Title: No immediate plans to amend laws on overloaded heavy vehicles, says Loke
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Transport Ministry has no immediate plans to amend laws on overloaded heavy vehicles as existing provisions are sufficient to address the offence.
Its minister Anthony Loke said the ministry would focus on firm and consistent enforcement, including action against repeat offenders, to protect road users and reduce road damage.
He said the Land Public Transport Agency had strengthened its punitive action matrix for operator offences, allowing it to suspend or revoke vehicle permits and operator licences based on the severity and recurrence of offences.
"Action against overloading covers drivers or vehicle owners, depending on the offence committed, as well as operators who breach licence conditions.
"For licensed operators, the Land Public Transport Act allows conditions to be imposed so that the weight of goods vehicles does not exceed the maximum limit," he said.
Loke was winding up the debate on the 2027 Supply Bill in the Dewan Rakyat.
He said operators who breached the conditions could be fined between RM1,000 and RM500,000, jailed for up to two years, or both, upon conviction.
Vehicles suspected of involvement in such offences could also be seized under the Act, he said.
"Forfeiture is subject to a court order under the same section.
"Administrative action on vehicle permits or operator licences can also be taken based on the offence and the company's record of violations," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ismail claims full support of all assemblymen
Article:
SEREMBAN: Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim said he had the full support of all 24 Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional assemblymen in leading the state government.
He said their support was evident in efforts to ensure the 2027 Negri Sembilan Budget was ready for tabling at the state legislative assembly sitting on Nov 27.
"Claims that I lack support are untrue. All 24 government assemblymen support me. We are focused on preparing the 2027 Negri Sembilan Budget.
"I also have the support of department heads, government assemblymen and former state executive council (Exco) members, although the latter are no longer part of the state administration.
"I hope everyone will cooperate so the state assembly can convene and the budget can be approved," he told reporters after visiting fire victims at a temporary relief centre at the Kampung Sekolah community hall in Gedong Lalang, Ampangan, here today.
Also present was Ampangan assemblyman Datuk Dr Mohamad Rafie Abd Malek.
Ismail said budget preparations were in their final stages, with civil servants, particularly department heads, working together to complete them.
He said there were no changes to the schedule, with the state assembly sitting set to be opened on Nov 26, followed by the Budget tabling on Nov 27.
On assistance for the fire victims, Ismail said the state government, through the Negri Sembilan Islamic Religious Council (Mains), would cover their rent for three months, with the assistance extendable to six months if necessary.
Four houses behind UTC Ampangan were destroyed in a fire on Sunday night.
Reports said the semi-permanent houses were almost 90 per cent destroyed. However, all eight occupants from three families escaped unharmed.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zahid confirms positive outcome in BN-MCA talks over Melaka seats
Article:
DURIAN TUNGGAL: Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has confirmed that special discussions with MCA leadership over Melaka election seat allocations ended positively.
Zahid, who is also deputy prime minister, said the discussions involved MCA president Datuk Seri Dr Wee Ka Siong, BN secretary-general Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir, and Melaka BN chairman and Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh.
However, he said an announcement on the outcome had been left to Ab Rauf, who was given the mandate to do so.
"The meeting with the MCA president, the Barisan Nasional secretary-general, and the Melaka chief minister showed positive developments.
"I cannot announce it as the Melaka chief minister has been given the mandate to make the announcement. Please direct follow-up questions to him," he said.
He said this after officiating the Jelita (Job Empowerment by Learning and Inclusive Technical Advancement) 12-Hour Intensive Acceleration Training programme at Universiti Teknikal Malaysia Melaka (UTeM) here today.
Previously, MCA was reported to have maintained that it would not recognise any candidate from the party announced by BN for the Melaka state election without the agreement of its top leadership.
Wee was reported to have said that announcing candidates without prior consultation and MCA's agreement was unacceptable, while alleging that seats previously contested by the party were given to others.
The development raised questions over the status of two MCA incumbents announced by BN on Saturday night, namely Datuk Ngwe Hee Sem for the Machap Jaya state seat and Datuk Lim Ban Hong for Klebang.
Commenting on the rejection of BN candidates in the Durian Tunggal and Pantai Kundor state seats, Zahid said the coalition would resolve the issue internally.
However, he did not expect the resolution to lead to a change of the candidates announced ahead of nomination day this Saturday.
"I do not see that happening (a change of candidates)... we will take internal steps to resolve this.
"In any by-election or state election, let alone a general election, issues like this arise, not only for BN but also for other coalition parties.
"This is common and we can find the best solution," he said.
BN previously decided to field candidates in 21 of the 28 Melaka state seats, with the remaining seven seats allocated to PAS and its strategic partners.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Drunk, drug-impaired drivers may be required to compensate victims
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Transport Ministry is proposing amendments to the Road Transport Act to require offenders convicted of driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs to compensate victims or their next of kin.
Transport Minister Anthony Loke said Section 426 of the Criminal Procedure Code already provided for compensation, but the proposal would make it an additional punishment alongside fines and imprisonment.
"The proposal would cover cases resulting in death, serious injury or permanent disability.
"The court would decide the compensation based on the facts, evidence and circumstances of each case.
"Compensation ordered against offenders would be separate from insurance payouts, and victims or their next of kin would retain the right to seek compensation from the offender's insurer through civil proceedings," he said
Loke was winding up the debate on the 2027 Supply Bill for his ministry in the Dewan Rakyat today.
He said the ministry acknowledged the challenge of collecting compensation from offenders who lacked the financial means to pay and was exploring suitable mechanisms to ensure victims and their families remained protected.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: AME Elite bags RM120mil BAC project
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: AME Elite Consortium Bhd has secured a RM120 million contract to build a manufacturing and testing facility for global cooling solutions provider BAC in Nilai, Negri Sembilan.
Its construction arm AME Construction Sdn Bhd received the contract from project owner Rock Link Sdn Bhd to develop a 30,000 sq m facility, which is scheduled for completion within 14 months.
The plant will serve as BAC's Asia Pacific regional technical hub, supporting demand for cooling systems used in data centres, artificial intelligence infrastructure and advanced semiconductor manufacturing.
Located in Kawasan Perindustrian Nilai, the development comprises a single-storey detached factory, a two-storey regional engineering office and ancillary support buildings.
The facility will manufacture closed-circuit cooling towers, adiabatic coolers, hybrid systems and liquid cooling solutions.
It will also house a climate-controlled laboratory for engineering teams to develop and test cooling technologies suited to tropical climates and high-density applications.
The project is designed to meet Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design (LEED) Gold and FM Approved standards.
AME Elite executive director and group chief executive officer Dylan Tan Teck Eng said demand for specialised industrial facilities was growing as global technology supply chains evolved.
He said the group's in-house construction capabilities enabled it to deliver technically complex facilities within accelerated timelines to meet multinational customers' requirements.
The latest award adds to AME Elite's external construction and engineering order book, which stood at RM485.7 million as at June 30, 2026, before the contract was secured.
The group has also undertaken projects in the aerospace and advanced technology sectors, reflecting demand for specialised industrial developments serving multinational companies.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man found drowned in Sungai Petani river
Article:
SUNGAI PETANI: A man who
fell into a river
in Kampung Padang Sekawan, Bukit Selambau, on Sunday has been found dead.
Mohamad Solihim Mohd Noor, 38, was found at 8.49am after members of the public reported the discovery, the Kedah Fire and Rescue Department's Operations Centre said.
His body was found floating near Kampung Belida Health Clinic, about 6km from the Lesung Fire and Rescue Control Post.
Six members of the Sungai Petani Fire and Rescue Station's Water Rescue Team were dispatched to the location.
His body was found caught on a fish cage about 200m from the riverbank.
His identity was confirmed by his mother.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: EAIC recommends action against Nada officers over raid SOP breaches
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Enforcement Agency Integrity Commission (EAIC) has recommended disciplinary action against National Anti-Drugs Agency (Nada) officers over negligence and breaches of standard operating procedures (SOPs) during a raid in Bera, Pahang.
In a statement, the EAIC said its investigation found that poor tactical handling and non-compliance with SOPs triggered panic and a scuffle that injured a civilian during an operation to detect suspected drug offenders on Oct 13 last year.
"The investigation found negligence in the tactical handling of the raid and non-compliance with SOPs by the Bera Nada operations team, which triggered panic and a scuffle resulting in injuries to a civilian or third party at the scene," the commission said.
The investigation, conducted under Section 27(4) of the Enforcement Agency Integrity Commission Act, also found that officers from the Bera Nada office had breached the agency director-general's standing orders, specifically PTKP BAB 02/2025 (Amendment 2026).
These included failing to record the scuffle or injuries in their official pocket notebooks and shortcomings in photographic documentation during the operation.
However, the EAIC said allegations that Nada officers had threatened those involved to prevent them from disclosing the incident to outsiders could not be substantiated.
The EAIC said the recommended disciplinary action fell under the Public Officers (Conduct and Discipline) Regulations.
It also called for an overhaul of operational procedures, including specific risk assessment guidelines and amendments to standing orders on officer identification during raids, lighting at operation sites and the mandatory recording of injuries.
The commission further recommended that Nada provide all enforcement personnel deployed for field operations with properly maintained pocket notebooks.
It also urged the Home Ministry to prioritise a policy on supplying and procuring body-worn cameras for Nada enforcement personnel conducting field operations.
The EAIC said it remained committed to strengthening integrity and professionalism among enforcement agencies under its supervision.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: EC to meet on Nov 6 to set key dates for Sarawak polls
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Election Commission (EC) will hold a special meeting on Nov 6 to discuss key dates for the 13th Sarawak state election.
EC secretary Datuk Khairul Shahril Idrus said the meeting would be chaired by EC chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun, with a press conference to be held immediately afterwards.
"The meeting will discuss key dates for the 13th Sarawak state election, including the issuance of election writs, nomination day and polling day, as well as the electoral roll to be used and other preparations for the election," he said in a statement today.
He said the EC had today received official notification from Sarawak State Legislative Assembly Speaker Tan Sri Mohamad Asfia Awang Nassar confirming the dissolution of the 19th Sarawak State Legislative Assembly, effective yesterday, in accordance with Article 21(2) of the State Constitution.
"Under Article 21(4) of the Sarawak State Constitution, an election must be held within 60 days of the dissolution," he said.
On Friday, Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg announced that the State Legislative Assembly would be dissolved effective Oct 26 to pave the way for the state election.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Negri Sembilan to remain without exco until court ruling, says MB
Article:
SEREMBAN: Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim has no plans to propose new state executive council (Exco) members until the dispute over their appointments is resolved in court.
He said the state government was currently operating without an exco line-up.
"We have taken the matter to court, so we will wait for its decision. There may be discussions and other developments, but I am not sure," he told reporters after visiting fire victims and presenting aid at a temporary relief centre at the Kampung Sekolah community hall in Gedung Lalang Ampangan here today.
Also present were Ampangan assemblyman Datuk Dr Mohamad Rafie Abd Malek, Seremban district officials and Social Welfare Department representatives.
Ismail was responding to questions about the state administration's lack of exco members and claims that some of the former exco members might withdraw their court application.
The appointments of all 10 Exco members, who had been sworn in before the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, at Istana Besar Seri Menanti, were revoked with effect from Sept 20. The revocation was gazetted on Sept 24.
Tuanku Muhriz withdrew his consent and revoked their appointments after stating that they had breached their loyalty pledge made during their swearing-in on Aug 7.
The former Exco members subsequently filed an application in the Federal Court to challenge the decision, naming the Negri Sembilan state secretary and state government as respondents.
The application was filed on Oct 14 through law firm Hafarizam Wan & Aisha Mubarak.
Asked about rumours that he would resign as menteri besar, Ismail, who is also the Juasseh assemblyman, dismissed them as unfounded.
"That is just a rumour," he said, adding that certain parties were deliberately circulating the claim, particularly on social media.
On reports that some former Exco members had yet to return their official vehicles despite instructions to do so following the revocation, Ismail said he was unaware of the matter.
"I don't know. I only look after my own car," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nik Nazmi spends over 3 hours giving statement to JAIS over khalwat case
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Former Setiawangsa member of parliament Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad today completed the recording of his statement with the Selangor Islamic Religious Department over a khalwat (close proximity) case.
His Syariah lawyer, Muhammad Amirul Ashraf A. Ghani, said Nik Nazmi had appeared before Jais to assist in investigations under Section 29 of the Syariah Criminal Offences (Selangor) Enactment 1995.
"We have fully cooperated with the investigation. The decision on whether to press charges rests with the Selangor Syariah Prosecution Department," he said outside Bangunan Sultan Idris Shah here.
Nik Nazmi, 44, arrived at the Jais office at about 9.15am and left at 1.30pm.
Jais director Datuk Mohd Shahzihan Ahmad confirmed that Nik Nazmi had appeared at the department but declined to comment further.
On Oct 15, Jais said an arrest had been made in connection with a suspected khalwat offence involving a political leader in the Petaling district at about 6pm.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Transport Ministry plans jail terms for rail cable thieves
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Transport Ministry plans to amend the Land Public Transport Act to impose heavier penalties, including jail terms, on those who steal cables from rail infrastructure.
Transport Minister Anthony Loke said a memorandum on the proposed amendments had been prepared and would be circulated for feedback before being submitted to the cabinet for policy approval.
He said he was confident the amendments could be tabled in Parliament at its first meeting next year, subject to cabinet approval.
"Cable theft is a major problem that we have discussed repeatedly with the Home Ministry and other parties.
"The Transport Ministry is taking steps to amend the Land Public Transport Act to increase penalties for cable theft, including imprisonment.
"Cable theft damages train systems and poses significant safety risks to the public," he said.
Loke was winding up the debate on the 2027 Supply Bill for his ministry in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Earlier, Datuk Dr Radzi Jidin (PN-Putrajaya) raised concerns over cable theft involving public transport infrastructure.
Radzi said an increasing number of rail services, including the Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) and Express Rail Link (ERL), had been affected by cable theft. He asked what medium- and long-term measures the government planned to take to address the problem.
He warned that billions of ringgit spent on public transport infrastructure could be undermined if cable theft continued.
In April, the New Straits Times reported that MRT infrastructure in the Klang Valley remained a
target for cable theft syndicates,
with 16 cases recorded since January resulting in losses of RM1.28 million.
Prasarana Group chief health, safety, security, environment and sustainable development officer Idzqandar Abu Bakar said the thefts persisted despite intensified patrols, the deployment of K-9 units and increased closed-circuit television surveillance along vulnerable stretches.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Northeast monsoon begins, raising flood risks in low-lying areas
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Low-lying areas along the peninsula's west coast face flood risks as the northeast monsoon begins today, with residents urged to heed weather warnings.
Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia (UKM) International Strategic and Sustainable Development Goals Consultancy Centre principal fellow Professor Dr Mohd Ekhwan Toriman said recent heavy rain had affected several areas, including Yan, Kuala Muda and Pendang in Kedah, as well as low-lying areas in Penang and Penampang, Sabah.
He said the northeast monsoon, expected to last until March next year, would bring strong winds, prolonged rain and rising sea levels along coastal areas.
"When heavy rain coincides with high tides, river water cannot flow into the sea, causing it to back up and overflow onto land and into residential drainage systems.
"This is compounded by poorly maintained drainage systems," he said when contacted today.
Universiti Malaysia Terengganu Faculty of Science and Marine Environment lecturer Dr Chung Jing Xiang said the monsoon might be less severe than usual as the country remained under the influence of El Niño.
However, he cautioned that this did not eliminate the need to monitor weather risks.
He said north-easterly winds blowing from continental Asia across the South China Sea would bring additional moisture, creating cloudy conditions and potentially triggering very heavy rain and major floods.
Cold surges accompanied by strong north-easterly winds could also bring torrential rain, particularly to the peninsula's east coast and the west coasts of Sabah and Sarawak.
Chung said the Borneo vortex, a low-pressure system that can develop over waters off Sabah and Sarawak, could trigger heavy rain in those areas. Under favourable conditions, it could move towards the peninsula and bring heavy rain to the east coast.
Meanwhile, Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) director-general Dr Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip said Kelantan, Pahang and Johor, as well as western Sarawak, were typically exposed to monsoon-related risks.
He said MetMalaysia had opened its operations room today to monitor conditions, with state offices nationwide involved.
Malaysia is expected to remain in the 2026/2027 northeast monsoon season until March 2027.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Health Service Commission bill targeted for tabling before end of 15th Parliament - Dzulkefly
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Ministry of Health (MOH) aims to obtain a policy decision from the Cabinet on the establishment of the Health Service Commission this year and, if approved, table the Bill in Parliament by the end of the 15th Parliament at the latest.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the establishment of the commission would further strengthen the management of human resources and the welfare of healthcare personnel, covering all 86 service schemes under the MOH.
He said the commission would not have the authority to create new positions, formulate the remuneration system or determine emolument rates, as these functions fall under the purview of the Public Service Department (PSD) and the Ministry of Finance.
"The commision's powers are subject to Article 144 of the Federal Constitution, namely matters relating to the power to appoint, confirm and place personnel in permanent or pensionable positions, promote, transfer and exercise disciplinary control over members of the service.
"Following this, the MOH held an engagement session with other service commissions and the PSD on Oct 22 to obtain further information on the duties and functions of the commission as well as the process for establishing it," he said during the question-and-answer session in the Dewan Rakyat today.
He was responding to a question from Datuk Seri Dr Zaliha Mustafa (PH-Sekijang), who asked about the minister's commitment to table the Health Service Commission Bill for its first reading by the end of 2027, in line with the reform aspirations of the 2023 Health White Paper.
Dzulkefly said the MOH continued to improve human resource-related matters through the establishment of the MOH Staffing Task Force with all central agencies.
"This includes the mandate given by the PSD to the MOH to manage the distribution of positions, the rates of payment for on-call duty allowances (ETAP), as well as the permanent appointment of 15,000 contract medical officers since 2023, including 9,000 permanent appointments specifically for 2027, which will ultimately bring an end to the contract doctor system.
"These are among our efforts to improve matters while moving towards the establishment of a Health Service Commission, as envisaged in the White Paper by the Health Reform Commission," he said.
In response to a supplementary question from Datuk Dr Alias Razak (PN-Kuala Nerus) on comprehensive reforms through the commission following the resignation of 3,510 medical officers between 2024 and 2026, he said the MOH had created a special quota of up to 30 per cent for opportunities to pursue specialist studies, specifically for medical officers serving in Sabah and Sarawak.
"We hope this commission will be able to resolve the legacy issues that I have inherited for so long. But today, we have already put in place several foundations for solutions, including increasing permanent positions," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Saifuddin quips he is 'envious' of Ngeh's vast Kelantan plantations
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail quipped that he was "envious" of Beruas member of parliament Datuk Ngeh Koo Ham's extensive plantations in Kelantan.
The remark came as Saifuddin wound up debate on the 2027 Supply Bill for the Home Ministry, following Ngeh's concerns over difficulties employers face in obtaining foreign worker quotas through the e-Quota system.
Ngeh said the cumbersome application process, which includes travelling to Putrajaya for interviews, had driven some employers to hire undocumented foreign workers.
"If the government can resolve this issue, I believe the influx of undocumented migrants can be reduced, as there would be no market for workers without proper documentation.
"Undocumented migrants would not come if employers could hire and pay foreign workers legally," he said.
Ngeh also questioned why applications and interviews could not be conducted online, noting that court proceedings were already held virtually.
"Why can't this simple application process be conducted online if courts can hold hearings online?
"Decisions on applications, whether approved or rejected, should be communicated within a month. At present, even after a year, applications may still not be approved. I urge the minister to resolve this issue," he said.
In response, Saifuddin said Ngeh had raised the matter not only as an MP but also as an employer seeking foreign workers for his plantations in Kelantan.
"Beruas is not speaking only as an MP, but also as an employer. He has submitted many applications for foreign workers for his plantations, which are extensive," he said.
"I am also envious of how he managed to acquire plantations in Kelantan," he added.
Ngeh then responded: "Please do not deflect from the issue. This is an issue that threatens public order in Malaysia."
Saifuddin subsequently withdrew his remark.
"Beruas, there will be a cabinet committee on foreign workers meeting tomorrow, chaired by Bagan Datuk (Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi), of which the Home Ministry is also a member.
"I promise to raise this matter at tomorrow's meeting for the committee's consideration," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Impact Capital sets 22 sen IPO price
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Impact Capital Holdings Bhd expects to raise RM21.27 million from its initial public offering (IPO) ahead of its planned listing on the ACE Market of Bursa Malaysia on Nov 24.
The information and communications technology (ICT) systems integrator's IPO comprises a public issue of 96.69 million new shares and an offer for sale of 28.62 million existing shares, at an issue price of 22 sen per share.
Managing director Winston Chai Fung Chun said the IPO will provide the group with additional financial resources to expand its operations, strengthen its technical capabilities and grow its workforce.
"The launch of our prospectus represents another important milestone as we progress towards becoming a public listed company and enter our next phase of growth," he said in a statement.
Impact Capital has about 21 years of operating experience through its subsidiaries, providing ICT equipment and systems integration for telecommunications infrastructure, enterprise networks, data centres, security systems and digital twin solutions.
It also supplies ICT hardware and software and provides maintenance and support, information technology service management implementation and managed network services.
Of the IPO proceeds, RM4.67 million will be allocated for office expansion, including a new Klang Valley office housing its Digital Innovation and Solutions Centre (DISC), relocation to larger offices in Bintulu and Kota Kinabalu, and the establishment of a new office in Johor Bahru.
Another RM4.53 million will fund workforce expansion and business development initiatives, while RM2.1 million will be used to enhance technology capabilities.
The company has allocated RM5.17 million for working capital and RM4.8 million for estimated listing expenses.
Chai said Impact Capital plans to establish the DISC as a platform for solution demonstrations, customer engagement and in-house technical validation.
"We will also increase our design and development activities, incorporating foundational data and AI software into our solutions to enhance their capabilities and deliver greater value to our customers," he said.
The company is expanding into digital twin solutions, which create virtual representations of physical assets, infrastructure and systems to enable real-time monitoring, simulation and operational optimisation.
It also plans to incorporate artificial intelligence (AI) and data-driven capabilities to support predictive analytics, asset management and decision-making.
According to the independent market research report by Vital Factor Consulting Sdn Bhd, Malaysia's information and communication services industry generated RM189.5 billion in revenue in 2025, growing at a compound annual growth rate of 5.4 per cent between 2023 and 2025.
Malaysia's digital economy accounted for 23.4 per cent of gross domestic product in 2024, the report said.
Applications for the IPO open today and close on Nov 6.
Upon listing, Impact Capital is expected to have a market capitalisation of RM105.6 million, based on the IPO price of 22 sen per share and an enlarged share capital of 480 million shares.
Public Investment Bank Bhd is the principal adviser, sponsor, sole underwriter and sole placement agent for the IPO.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Indonesia deploys 'oxygen bus' as forest-fire haze chokes residents
Article:
PALANGKA RAYA, Indonesia: A bus fitted out with oxygen tanks is providing a sanctuary in a city on Indonesia's Borneo island where people are choking from forest-fire-induced haze and the blazes show no sign of letting up.
Indonesia regularly battles seasonal forest fires, predominantly on Sumatra and Borneo islands, but this year the infernos are the most intense in more than a decade.
An intense El Nino weather phenomenon has driven up temperatures, leaving the country's vast forests and peatlands more vulnerable to fires that have turned skies orange across Indonesia, Malaysia and Singapore.
As respiratory illnesses increased in the Central Kalimantan city of Palangka Raya, the local government provided an 'oxygen bus' replete with oxygen tanks and medical professionals who offer residents a chance to be hooked up to a small oxygen tube around their nose for 5 to 10 minutes at a time.
"The service is intended to help people access oxygen, particularly those experiencing respiratory problems or who need oxygen support amid unhealthy air quality conditions," the Central Kalimantan provincial health department said on Instagram this week.
Indonesia's air pollution index has shown some areas of Borneo and Sumatra registering pollution levels of over 1,000, with readings of 300 or more already categorised as hazardous.
Respiratory illnesses linked to the fires have risen, with about 350,000 cases from August to Oct 25, the health ministry said. Central Kalimantan reported about 31,000 cases as of Oct 25.
"This is a disaster from nature and there is not much we can do," Oktawina, 44, who like many Indonesians goes by one name, said with an oxygen tube hooked to her nose.
Medical staff on the white-and-blue bus recorded patients' details and administered oxygen to residents reporting breathing difficulties. One of them, Yuda, said most residents who came to the bus coughing or had trouble breathing.
Purnasari, 31, another patient on the bus, said: "If I've been out of the house lately I feel tightness and coughing ... because this morning the thick yellowish smoke so my breathing feels tight."
Hundreds of students protested at the office of the provincial governor last week demanding a greater response to the fires, local news website Kompas reported.--REUTERS
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man charged with flashing private parts to 12-year-old girl in condominium lift
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A construction worker pleaded not guilty at the Sessions Court to exposing himself to a 12-year-old girl in a condominium lift.
Muhammad Aniq Mohd Jafri, 25, is accused of committing the offence at a condominium in Taman Danau Desa between 6.30pm and 6.50pm on April 1.
The charge, under Section 15(a)(i) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017, carries a maximum 10-year jail term, a fine of up to RM20,000, or both, upon conviction.
Aniq entered his plea before judge Suhaila Haron.
Deputy public prosecutor V. Suloshani sought bail of RM10,000 with one surety and asked the court to impound the accused's passport and require him to report to a police station monthly.
"The accused should also be barred from contacting or interfering with the victim and prosecution witnesses until case disposal," she said.
Aniq, who was unrepresented, appealed for a lower bail amount.
Suhaila granted him bail of RM9,000 with one surety and imposed the additional conditions requested by the prosecution.
The court fixed Nov 30 for mention.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Four foreign boys detained over intimidation of 71-year-old woman
Article:
BUKIT MERTAJAM: Four foreign boys aged between nine and 12 have been detained following a criminal intimidation report lodged by a 71-year-old woman in Taman Sri Rambai.
Seberang Prai Tengah district police chief Assistant Commissioner Nik Aminuddin Raja Abdullah said police received the report yesterday over an incident outside the woman's home on Oct 22 at 6pm.
He said the woman had reprimanded a group of children playing at a nearby playground for making excessive noise.
However, she alleged that the group ignored her warning and threw stones and a metal rod at her.
"The objects did not hit her, but the incident left her frightened and prompted her to lodge a police report," he said in a statement today.
Following investigations, police detained the four boys in separate operations around Taman Sri Rambai and seized several items believed to be linked to the incident.
Nik Aminuddin said the boys were brought before the Bukit Mertajam Magistrate's Court, where a four-day remand order was obtained from Oct 27 to 30 to facilitate further investigations.
The case is being investigated under Section 506 of the Penal Code, Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63 and Section 14 of the Minor Offences Act 1955.
He advised parents and guardians to monitor their children's behaviour and teach them to respect others.
He also called on the public to maintain good neighbourly relations and report any threats to public safety to the police.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Dr Siti Hawa's mother recalls final days of SMA scholar who defied odds
Article:
KUANTAN: Dr Siti Hawa Apandi, the country's first spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) patient to complete four levels of higher education at a single university, spent much of her final days resting in bed.
Her mother, Zaidah Tamjis, 64, said Siti Hawa, 37, had been resting more than usual at their home in Taman Seri Mahkota Aman here, instead of following her routine of sitting for long periods while using her laptop.
In August,
Siti Hawa
was recognised by the Malaysia Book of Records for completing her diploma, bachelor's degree, master's degree and PhD at Universiti Malaysia Pahang Al-Sultan Abdullah (UMPSA).
"Over the past two to three days, she said she was tired and wanted to lie down. She would sit up to have her milk before lying down again about half an hour later.
"When I asked if she wanted to use her laptop, she said no," Zaidah told reporters when met today.
She said her daughter, the third of five siblings, received milk through a feeding tube about 6pm yesterday but refused another serving around 10pm.
"I tried to wake her about 5.30am but she did not respond. I called an ambulance, and the medical team later confirmed her death," she said.
One of Zaidah's most painful memories was when Siti Hawa was admitted to the intensive care unit at Tengku Ampuan Afzan Hospital here last year with a bacterial infection.
"The family could not stay with her, so she was alone. We were only allowed to visit during visiting hours," said Zaidah, who had always stayed by her daughter's side, even moving into a hostel at UMPSA in 2007.
Despite her grief, Zaidah said she was immensely proud of her daughter's academic achievements, which had brought some of the happiest moments of her and her husband's lives.
"I am grateful that my daughter achieved her ambition of excelling in her studies. I accept that God has everything planned for us," she said.
The New Straits Times previously reported that Zaidah had made the hostel at UMPSA's Gambang campus her second home for about a decade after Siti Hawa enrolled in a diploma programme in 2007.
She remained by her daughter's side throughout her degree studies.
During a previous interview, Zaidah said she had never considered giving up, believing her daughter's determination deserved equal strength from a mother's
unconditional love.
SMA is a genetic disorder that damages motor neurons in the spinal cord, progressively weakening the muscles they control.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Penang holds developer, landowner responsible for fatal landslide, warns of legal action
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: The Penang government has held the developer and landowner of a condominium and road project responsible for the
fatal landslide
that killed a 73-year-old doctor.
Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow warned of possible legal consequences, saying the landslide occurred on the developer's land and that the parties were responsible for site safety and mitigation measures.
"The landowner and developer must take responsibility for the effects of the landslide, including legal implications, approval-related matters and mitigation works to restore site safety," he said when met at the scene.
The Penang Island City Council (MBPP) has issued an immediate stop-work order and given the developer seven days to submit a mitigation plan to secure the site and prevent further soil movement, he added.
The state government had received reports from MBPP and the Penang Town and Country Planning Department, as well as a draft incident report from the council's engineering department.
"The final report is expected within one or two days," he said.
Chow said preliminary findings indicated that slope stabilisation works had begun, but the landslide occurred in an area where the work had yet to be carried out.
He said several days of rain could have caused surface runoff to seep into the soil, increasing the load on the unstabilised slope and triggering the landslide.
However, the authorities would await the full report before establishing the circumstances of the incident, he added.
On possible legal action, Chow said affected parties were entitled to pursue legal remedies against those responsible.
"This country does not prohibit any party affected by an act of commission or omission from taking appropriate legal action," he said, adding that police were at the scene.
The state government and MBPP would also provide assistance, including legal support where necessary, to the victim's family, he added.
Chow expressed condolences to the family of Dr Wong Kar Lin, who died in the incident, and said the authorities would continue to work with them on the necessary follow-up measures.
Residents of neighbouring homes affected by the landslide would only be allowed to return after the relevant disaster management authorities had assessed the site, particularly the slope's stability, said Chow.
Addressing concerns over the project's approval history and residents' earlier objections, he said the hillside development had a planning approval history dating back to 1996, with changes in land ownership, developers and development guidelines over the years.
He said the latest developer obtained approval in 2023 after fulfilling technical requirements, including those relating to environmental impact, traffic and social impact, and following the outcome of appeal proceedings.
"The local authority does not grant approvals arbitrarily, but in accordance with the Town and Country Planning Act and the relevant technical requirements.
"In this case, all requirements have been met, with the project approval having followed all the necessary processes," he said.
Chow said the original approval covered townhouses and a 16-storey block.
The site had since undergone various changes, including proceedings before the Appeals Board, which rejected an appeal against the project.

Title: EV sales are picking up, but is the after sales support ready to service the market?
Article:
GIVEN the current sales trend of the Proton e.MAS brand, which clocked just over 32,000 sales in 2026, it looks like electrified vehicles have gained enough traction to break the 10 per cent barrier sometime in the final quarter of this year.
This is certainly good news to the ears of the government, which has been struggling with high fuel prices and ballooning subsidies while the Malaysian motorist gets access to some of the best electric models from China at affordable prices.
As the number of electric vehicles ramps up quickly, there will be additional strain on the after sales network with more problems cropping up and more types of issues to troubleshoot just by virtue of statistics.
While crossing the 10 per cent mark is a significant data point, crossing it is far from a guarantee that electric drive technology will continue to gain acceptance and make it into the mainstream in the next year; that timeline may stretch well to the early 2030s.
When a new technology is introduced to the world, it may lay dormant or remain as a novelty for some years before slowly gaining public interest.
Cars are so ubiquitous now that we cannot imagine people rejecting them as an idea, but together with cellphones, computers, and colour televisions, they were among technologies that faced strong resistance, each taking around 20 years or more before entering the inflection point.
An inflection point is a sudden up curve in the demand for the technology that indicates it has passed a threshold and now has a very real chance of becoming mainstream. This point typically sits around 12 to 15 per cent of total market volume.
Globally, battery electric vehicles (BEV) crossed that threshold some three years ago.
While Norway showed the way when it comes to mass adoption in 2020, it was the Chinese automotive market - the biggest in the world - that did most of the volume lifting.
In practical terms, the global automotive industry can no longer turn back the tide to pure internal combustion engines (ICE), as total BEV and plug-in hybrid electric vehicle sales broke the 50 per cent barrier in September, with both technologies on very similar footing.
Malaysia is a technology consumer and has very little voice in determining what we actually get to buy in our own market.
The shrinking global ICE market means the number of pure ICE model launches will quickly shrink to nothing within the next few years, with only the special sports car market holding on to the emotional value of an exhaust note and petrol fumes.
While we cannot control the technology coming into the market, poor after sales support will slow down the transition, and that deceleration can have significant financial and planning consequences for the entire industry.
Increased acceptance of BEVs and PHEVs will be determined by ease of maintenance and reasonable costs for maintenance and replacement parts.
In this regard, Proton New Energy Technology, or Pro-Net, has the biggest problem because they have the highest number of cars on the road.
Transitioning ICE service technicians to EVs is not as simple as handing them a multimeter and a few new tools.
The skillset and risk profiles are fundamentally different, and a single careless move with a high-voltage orange cable or connector can result in severe electrocution.
A rigorous training framework is essential to ensure this transition happens safely.
Recognising this critical risk factor, Proton partnered with TVET Mara and its Masjid Tanah campus to strengthen its upskilling programme and develop a formal certification process for EV technicians and service advisors.
During their inaugural EV technician and service advisor competition recently, we had a chance to see what it takes to be certified.
The high voltage electric system presents very different risks and demands very specific steps to manage them, including the workshop environment, personal protective gear, specialised insulated tools and, most importantly, detailed Standard Operating Procedures that must be adhered to strictly to prevent injury, or worse.
With a population of 40,000 vehicles, Pro-Net now has over 160 technicians manning 46 service centres, which looks a bit sparse, but thankfully most of the e.Mas on our roads are less than a year old and are not even due for their first scheduled visit to a service centre.
Right now, Proton trains their technicians in-house and TVET Mara conducts the evaluation process. Having third-party assessment ensures better quality technicians passing through the gate.
Above and beyond training their own technicians, the collaboration with TVET Mara has resulted in an EV module that is now an optional part of their automotive technology diploma.
For youngsters who are interested, it's important to note that right now, the EV-specific module can only be introduced at the diploma level as it requires a rigorous foundation in automotive technology.
Proton's own training involves various modules covering the battery, motor, software, and other aspects. Each module takes a few days of training, so the programme is quite extensive and intensive.
They say the Human Resource Development Ministry and the relevant departments within it that develop training curricula and modules are working together with carmakers to develop a course that can be deployed in various training institutions, such as the Advanced Technology Training Centres, which are available nationwide.
The courses have just been introduced, and we can expect graduates to start entering the workforce from next year onwards.
This is good news for the automotive industry, and hopefully, as all the training programmes move as planned, we can start to see opportunities for our younger generation during this challenging time of transition.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MASFIH wants federal aid for families of 54 missing Malaysians
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Solidarity Families in Hope (MASFIH) wants the government to provide humanitarian aid to families of 54 Malaysians missing in Nepal and appoint Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan to coordinate assistance.
MASFIH coordinator and spokesperson Dr Manivannan Rethinam said he had contacted all cabinet ministers via WhatsApp and email ahead of the Oct 23 meeting to seek support for the proposals.
He said several ministers had responded positively.
The first proposal calls for the Finance Ministry to lead a whole-of-government effort to help families deal with banks, insurers, takaful operators, Bursa Malaysia, unit trusts, the Companies Commission of Malaysia and the Employees Provident Fund (EPF), among other institutions.
Manivannan said families were struggling to obtain essential financial information and manage their missing relatives' financial obligations because they could not obtain the usual consent or authorisation.
"MASFIH is not asking for existing laws to be disregarded. We seek a lawful, accountable and compassionate mechanism to assess exceptional cases with appropriate safeguards," he said.
He proposed that the minister chair an initial coordination meeting with MASFIH and relevant agencies, followed by a progress review within 30 days.
The second proposal seeks substantial, one-off federal humanitarian assistance for all 54 families to cover essential living expenses and protect their livelihoods for six to 12 months.
Manivannan said many households had lost their main or sole breadwinner and were struggling with daily expenses, loan commitments, education costs and business obligations.
"Their immediate needs cannot reasonably be postponed until documentation, legal procedures or estate administration are completed.
"The assistance needs to be distributed equitably, regardless of race, ethnicity or religion, with the government determining the appropriate amount, eligibility criteria and delivery mechanism," he said.
MASFIH welcomed reported progress in expediting documentation for the missing persons, including an assurance conveyed by Nepal's prime minister to his Malaysian counterpart.
However, Manivannan said financial assistance and national coordination should proceed in parallel, as resolving legal and estate-related matters could take months.
"This is prudent contingency planning, not a lack of confidence in Nepal's efforts," he said.
He added that the missing persons should not automatically be presumed dead, as their families continued to hope for their safe return.
Manivannan acknowledged Malaysia's US$1 million contribution towards Nepal's rebuilding efforts but said MASFIH understood that the affected families had yet to receive federal humanitarian assistance specifically addressing their circumstances.
"As the next of kin of my younger sister, Komathi Rethinam, who also remains missing, I understand personally the pain of waiting without answers and the anxiety of not knowing what lies ahead.
"We are not asking the government to resolve every legal and administrative issue overnight.
"We are asking for clear leadership, coordinated action and meaningful assistance to begin now, while the necessary processes continue," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: RM14.3mil returned to online scam victims
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A total of RM14.3 million has been recovered and returned to online scam victims between Oct 12, 2022 and September this year.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the National Scam Response Centre (NSRC) acted on victims' complaints to stop funds from being moved through multiple bank accounts before they could be withdrawn or transferred elsewhere.
However, he said the amount recovered remained insufficient given the substantial losses suffered by scam victims.
"Are we satisfied with this? The answer is no, because losses resulting from online scams remain substantial," he said during the winding-up session for the 2027 Supply Bill for the Home Ministry.
From Oct 12, 2022 to August this year, the NSRC's 997 hotline received 468,675 calls involving reported losses totalling RM1.2 billion, he said.
Saifuddin said police had intensified intelligence gathering and enforcement operations against online scam syndicates.
Between 2024 and last month, police conducted 968 raids and arrested 7,262 people.
"Further profiling revealed that 2,912 of those arrested had records indicating they had previously worked or stayed in Cambodia, a country associated with such activities.
"This is a significant finding. The information will help strengthen intelligence gathering and monitoring of transnational criminal syndicates.
"We are also intensifying international cooperation through Interpol, Aseanapol and bilateral police-to-police channels," he said.
On organised crime syndicates using Malaysia as an operational base, Saifuddin said police had stepped up intelligence gathering, operations and raids targeting premises identified as scam call centres.
He said enforcement efforts targeted not only operators but also the syndicates' wider operational structures.
From 2023 to August this year, arrests linked to call centres included 36 masterminds, 74 managers, 165 supervisors, 118 financial personnel handling mule accounts, 18 communications personnel, 132 IT programmers, 8,500 operators and 157 general workers.
"This approach aims to dismantle the command, technical, communications and financial networks that enable these syndicates to operate within the country," he added.
During the same period, police conducted 61,363 operations, said Saifuddin.
Police recorded 18,393 arrests in 2023, 12,278 in 2024, 23,753 in 2025 and 16,740 from January to August this year.
"These figures illustrate the scale of this emerging form of crime and the seriousness of the threat it poses," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: US midterms: 470 seats up for grabs in US$12bil election battle
Article:
WASHINGTON: Americans go to the polls on Nov 3 for elections that will shape the final two years of Donald Trump's presidency – although the president himself will not be on any ballot.
The "midterms," held halfway through a president's four-year term, decide control of Congress as well as governorships and thousands of state-level offices.
A Democratic takeover of either chamber would constrain Trump's agenda and bring greater congressional scrutiny of his administration; Republican victories would preserve the party's control in Washington.
Here is a look at the 2026 showdown by the numbers:
- HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES -
435:
Every seat in the House, the lower chamber of Congress, is contested every two years.
218:
The magic number for a majority in the 435-seat chamber.
3:
The net number of seats Democrats need to gain to take control. In 2024, Republicans won a 220-215 majority, although deaths, resignations and a party switch mean the current House stands at 218 Republicans, 214 Democrats, one independent and two vacancies.
For Republicans, that means a net loss of two seats is survivable. Three is not.
- SENATE AND THE STATES -
35:
Senate seats being contested – 33 in the normal six-year rotation plus special elections in Florida and Ohio.
Republicans now hold a 53-47 advantage in the 100-seat chamber, counting two independents who vote with the Democrats. Democrats therefore need a net gain of four seats to reach the 51 required for control; a 50-50 tie would be broken by Republican Vice President JD Vance.
36:
States electing governors, nearly three-quarters of the total.
6,139:
State legislative seats being regularly contested, across 88 of the country's 99 state legislative chambers.
- WHAT THE POLLS SAY -
53-41 per cent:
The Democratic advantage over Republicans among registered voters asked which party's congressional candidate they would support, in a PBS News/NPR/Marist poll conducted Sept 14-15.
The same survey found Democrats ahead among independent voters by 57 per cent to 32 per cent.
32-41 per cent:
The range of Trump's approval rating in several major September surveys.
Reuters/Ipsos put him at 31 per cent among US adults last week, the lowest of his political career, while Marist recorded 39 per cent and NBC News 41 per cent among registered voters. The surveys use different methodologies and populations, so the figures are not directly comparable – but none suggests an abundance of presidential coattails.
55 per cent:
Registered voters who told NBC News that Trump's policies had hurt the economy, against 26 percent who said he had helped it.
- MONEY, MONEY, MONEY -
ABOUT US$12 BILLION:
The amount expected to be spent on advertising during the 2025-26 election cycle.
Ad-tracking company AdImpact forecasts US$11.6 billion, exceeding both the previous midterm record of US$8.9 billion in 2022 and even the 2024 presidential cycle.
Kinetiq Political Insights' latest estimate is slightly higher at US$11.96 billion, with a projected range of US$11.5 billion to US$12.5 billion.
US$330 MILLION:
Advertising spending in the California governor's primary alone, according to AdImpact – making the preliminary contest to choose November's candidates the most expensive gubernatorial race on record.
And that was merely the warm-up.
- FOR THE TRIVIA FILE -
2,497:
Candidates who ran in US congressional primaries this year, the most in any election cycle since at least 2014. The vast majority – 2,232 of them – were chasing House seats.
44:
House races on Nov 3 that are rematches between the same major-party candidates who fought for the seat in 2024.
Broaden the search to state and local contests and there are 474 electoral rematches nationwide – proving that in American politics, as in Hollywood, there is rarely any objection to a sequel.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Saifuddin: No cover-up in death of man in police custody
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: There has been no attempt to cover up the case of Noorizwan Zulkefly, who died in police custody, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
He said the case had been taken over by the Criminal Investigation Department.
"The Home Ministry has never compromised on any violations.
"The same principle applies to everyone, including those who are considered rational and capable of distinguishing right from wrong. We will apply the same principle consistently.
"There has been no attempt to cover up this case," he said during the winding-up debate on the 2027 Supply Bill for the Home Ministry in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Noorizwan, 42, was detained on Sept 19 to assist investigations into drug possession, theft and housebreaking.
He was referred to Canselor Tuanku Muhriz Hospital in Cheras on Sept 30 and pronounced dead on Oct 1.
Earlier, Noorizwan's family, accompanied by lawyers and representatives of non-governmental organisations, marched from the National Monument to Parliament to submit a memorandum.
It was handed over to Saifuddin's political secretary, Omar A. Manap.
Also present were Pasir Gudang member of paliament (MP) Hassan Abdul Karim, Jelutong MP RSN Rayer, Bentong MP Young Syefura Othman, Bukit Bendera MP Syerleena Abdul Rashid and Beruas MP Datuk Ngeh Koo Ham.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Wan Saiful accuses Bersatu of being 'Trojan horse' within PN
Article:
KOTA BARU: Datuk Wan Saiful Wan Jan has accused Bersatu of being a "Trojan horse" within Perikatan Nasional (PN) and called for disciplinary action against the party.
The Parti Wawasan Negara vice-president also accused Bersatu secretary-general Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali of echoing DAP's narrative by suggesting that Pas was incapable of managing the coalition.
Wan Saiful claimed that Azmin and Bersatu were advancing DAP's agenda by spreading what he described as false propaganda about Pas' leadership of PN.
"The fact is, when Bersatu was leading PN, its supporters included people like us and Pas, who had no hidden agenda to weaken the coalition from within.
"But when Pas took over the leadership, Bersatu failed to be a good follower and instead plotted to weaken PN from within," he said.
The Tasek Gelugor member of parliament said PN's membership had expanded from four to six parties under Pas' leadership, following the entry of Wawasan and Pejuang, which he described as a success.
He said Bersatu's actions in several states showed that it was working against PN's interests.
"In Johor and Negri Sembilan, they fought against PN.
"In Pahang, they signed an agreement with the state government without PN's approval.
"In Selangor, it has been reported that they are negotiating an agreement with the Pakatan Harapan state government," he said.
Wan Saiful also accused Bersatu of repeatedly amplifying DAP's claims about Pas' weaknesses.
He said Bersatu had failed to attend PN Supreme Council meetings despite being invited, although the party had previously complained to the Registrar of Societies (RoS) that it had not been invited to meetings.
"All these show that Bersatu is a 'Trojan horse' working to weaken PN from within. They are actively working against the coalition's interests.
"Hence, they should face disciplinary action," he said.
Yesterday, Azmin criticised Pas secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan over his statement that PN would take disciplinary action against Bersatu.
Azmin also blamed Pas for the coalition's dispute with the RoS, saying the
party had "wrecked" PN.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Japan rape trial of ex-senior prosecutor resumes after two-year pause
Article:
TOKYO: The trial of a Japanese former senior prosecutor accused of rape in one of the country's most high-profile cases of alleged sexual assault restarted on Tuesday after a two-year pause.
Few women in Japan speak out about sexual assault, but a former prosecutor, who uses the pseudonym Hikari, came forward in 2024 to accuse her boss of raping her six years earlier.
The trial first began in October 2024 but was halted after Kentaro Kitagawa – who served as head of the Osaka District Public Prosecutor's Office at the time of the alleged rape – withdrew his initial admission of guilt and said the sex was consensual.
On Tuesday Kitagawa told the court that sex took place but repeated his not guilty plea and "denied that she was unable to resist", according to public broadcaster NHK.
Following his plea change, the court, prosecution and defence spent two years in closed-door proceedings clarifying the points at issue.
Hikari, who has been diagnosed with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), has previously said she was not used to drinking strong alcohol and lost her memory halfway through an office gathering in 2018.
The next thing she knew, she said, she was in Kitagawa's home and was being raped.
"It was like I was having a terrible nightmare," Hikari said in a 2025 interview with AFP.
"I couldn't resist because I was terrified that I could be killed."
Hikari kept quiet after it happened as Kitagawa had pleaded with her not to go public, saying it would be a damaging scandal for the organisation and threatening to harm himself, she said.
Hikari said her condition worsened after she learned in 2024 that people close to Kitagawa, especially an assistant prosecutor – who Hikari says is his lover – had spread malicious rumours about her.
Hikari has repeatedly requested an independent probe into harassment within prosecutor's offices across the country.
Officials have rejected that request and instead announced the launch in June of their own internal investigation.
Her request for measures to ensure a safe working environment was also rejected, prompting her to officially resign in August. --AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Maybank Islamic, CGC launch first supply chain financing guarantee scheme
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Maybank Islamic Bhd has teamed up with Credit Guarantee Corporation Malaysia Bhd (CGC) to introduce Malaysia's first supply chain financing guarantee scheme anchored by mid-tier companies (MTCs).
Under the collaboration, Maybank Islamic will provide Syariah-compliant supply chain financing facilities, while CGC will extend guarantee support to eligible MTCs under its BizJamin-i Mid-Tier Companies scheme.
The innovative structure, which forms part of Maybank's new economy ecosystem initiative, enables suppliers within MTC ecosystems, predominantly micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), to access early payment against approved invoices.
One of the key features is CGC's guarantee support, which enables eligible MTCs to act as anchors in their supply chains, allowing their suppliers to access financing against approved invoices.
Additionally, guarantee charges are transaction-based, with payments made only when the facility is used.
Maybank Islamic group chief executive officer (CEO) Mohamad Yasin Abdullah said the collaboration reflects the bank's commitment to humanising financial services by addressing the real financing needs of businesses across the supply chain.
"By combining Shariah-compliant financing with CGC's guarantee support, we are enabling MTCs and their suppliers to strengthen liquidity, build greater resilience and enhance their competitiveness.
"It also supports Maybank Group Islamic Banking's ROAR30 strategy to mobilise Islamic finance to drive real economic growth and elevate community wellbeing through values-based intermediation."
CGC president and CEO Mohamed Nazri Omar said a viable business is often turned away not because it lacks potential, but because the financier cannot see enough to proceed with confidence.
"Closing that gap is CGC's purpose. Through BizJamin-i, we are extending our guarantee to MTCs acting as anchors in their own supply chains, enabling the suppliers behind them, most of whom are MSMEs, to access financing against approved invoices rather than collateral they may not hold.
"When a supplier's trading record is visible and verifiable, our guarantee can reach further and support businesses that might otherwise be underserved," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Mahathir weighs next move on Dec 4 in RM150mil Anwar defamation suit
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad will inform the High Court on Dec 4 how he intends to proceed with his RM150 million defamation suit against Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
Dr Mahathir's lawyer, Muhammad Rafique Rashid Ali, said he had asked the court to give his client time to decide how to proceed in view of his current condition.
"We are all aware of Dr Mahathir's condition. I have asked the court to give him time and space to decide on the way forward.
"We will return to court on Dec 4 for case management to inform the court of his next step," he said.
The case management will be held before judicial commissioner Datuk Donald Joseph Franklin, who has been presiding over the trial.
Rafique also raised concerns about Dr Mahathir's fitness and stamina, given his age and medical condition.
He had considered applying for the proceedings to be conducted online and for the scope of cross-examination to be limited.
Dr Mahathir was absent from the SG4 Business and Economic Forum 2026 at the Kuala Lumpur Convention Centre yesterday due to ill health.
The trial was put on hold in January after Dr Mahathir suffered a fall.
He was admitted to the National Heart Institute on Jan 6 for observation and treatment. He turned 101 on July 10.
In the suit, Dr Mahathir alleges that Anwar defamed him by accusing him of being racist and enriching himself and his family during his 22-year tenure as prime minister.
Dr Mahathir claimed the statements were made during a speech at PKR's special national congress at Stadium Melawati in Shah Alam on March 18, 2023.
Anwar allegedly referred to an individual who had been in power for "22 years and an additional 22 months", accusing the person of using his position to enrich himself and his family.
Dr Mahathir is seeking RM100 million in exemplary damages and RM50 million in general damages. He is also seeking a written apology and a special press conference at which Anwar would publicly apologise for the alleged defamatory statements.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MBPP advised project consultant on slope safety months before fatal landslide
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: The Penang Island City Council (MBPP) had advised the consultant for the development project linked to Sunday's fatal landslide to take slope safety precautions in August.
Mayor Datuk A. Rajendran said the council had advised the project consultant following a site visit that month.
"We advised the consultant in August after a site visit and followed up with a letter on the measures that need to be taken at the site.
"They have put in place whatever measures required of them," he said when contacted.
He did not elaborate on the measures.
Rajendran said MBPP had visited all sites with slopes between August and September to advise those involved to take the necessary precautions ahead of the monsoon season.
He said investigations into the incident were ongoing.
"It is only right that I submit the report to the investigation committee," he said when asked about the probe and its initial findings.
The development project was issued a stop-work order following Sunday's landslide.
The project, which involves the construction of a road and apartments, has been ongoing for more than a year.
The incident
claimed the life
of 73-year-old Dr Wong Kar Lin. His wife and mother-in-law survived.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Fix your water supply before chasing RM720b GDP dream, Akmal tells SG4 states
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — Chronic deficits in basic utilities, highlighted by Kedah's zero per cent water reserve margin, will derail the ambitious long-term economic targets set by the four opposition-led SG4 states, Economy Minister Akmal Nasir warned today.
In a Facebook post while attending a Gas Exporting Countries Forum meeting in Moscow, Akmal commented on the SG4 Business & Economic Forum 2026, which projected a combined gross domestic product of RM723.75 billion for Kedah, Kelantan, Terengganu, and Perlis by 2050, an expansion that implies annual growth rates of up to 7 per cent.
While declining to dispute the headline figure directly, Akmal stressed that achieving such rapid expansion cannot rely on “Business as usual”, requiring rigorous planning, productivity gains, and disciplined project delivery on the ground.
The minister argued that persistent basic infrastructure deficits present a far more urgent obstacle to growth than setting economic projections, pointing to Kedah's depleted water reserve margin and longstanding clean water disruptions in Kelantan.
“How can the local economy be developed and investment attracted more vigorously without basic infrastructure facilities like this?” he asked.
Akmal stressed that industrialisation across the northern and east coast corridors relies overwhelmingly on federal financing rather than state coffers.
Federal development expenditure in the four states reached RM7.70 billion in 2025, approximately 6.8 times their combined state development allocations of roughly RM1.13 billion.
Under the 13th Malaysia Plan spanning 2026 to 2030, Putrajaya has approved 1,487 development projects valued at RM71.52 billion for the SG4 group. The federal spending ceiling for these states under Rolling Plan 2 for 2027 has been raised to RM8.11 billion, up 1.6 per cent from RM7.98 billion in 2026.
Federal agencies, he noted, continue to anchor the region's core industrial nodes, including the East Coast Rail Link, Kedah Rubber City, Tok Bali Industrial Park, Kertih Biopolymer Park, Perlis Inland Port, and Chuping Valley Industrial Area.
Addressing commercial inflows, Akmal cited Malaysian Investment Development Authority data recording RM37.23 billion in approved investments and 18,319 potential jobs across the four states in 2025.
“However, investment approval does not mean the project is complete. Potential jobs do not mean jobs have been created.
“We must ensure projects are truly implemented, local entrepreneurs take part in the supply chain, and the people get quality jobs and better incomes,” he said.
Akmal ended by saying that while the federal government continues to channel billions into catalytic infrastructure across the SG4 territories, state administrations must resolve foundational utility bottlenecks like water supply to support sustained industrial investment.

Title: Dzulkefly: Health Service Commission Bill to be tabled by end of 15th Parliament if approved
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) aims to obtain a policy decision from the Cabinet on the establishment of the Health Service Commission (SPK) this year and, if approved, table the Bill in Parliament by the end of the 15th Parliament at the latest.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad said the establishment of the commission would further strengthen the management of human resources and the welfare of healthcare personnel, covering all 86 service schemes under the MOH.
He said the SPK would not have the authority to create new positions, formulate the remuneration system or determine emolument rates, as these functions fall under the purview of the Public Service Department (JPA) and the Ministry of Finance.
“The SPK’s powers are subject to Article 144 of the Federal Constitution, namely matters relating to the power to appoint, confirm and place personnel in permanent or pensionable positions, promote, transfer and exercise disciplinary control over members of the service.
“Following this, the MOH held an engagement session with other service commissions and the JPA on Oct 22 to obtain further information on the duties and functions of the commission as well as the process for establishing it,” he said during the question-and-answer session in the Dewan Rakyat today.
He was responding to a question from Datuk Seri Dr Zaliha Mustafa (PH-Sekijang), who asked about the minister’s commitment to table the Health Service Commission Bill for its first reading by the end of 2027, in line with the reform aspirations of the 2023 Health White Paper.
Dzulkefly said the MOH continued to improve human resource-related matters through the establishment of the MOH Staffing Task Force with all central agencies.
“This includes the mandate given by the JPA to the MOH to manage the distribution of positions, the rates of payment for on-call duty allowances (ETAP), as well as the permanent appointment of 15,000 contract medical officers since 2023, including 9,000 permanent appointments specifically for 2027, which will ultimately bring an end to the contract doctor system.
“These are among our efforts to improve matters while moving towards the establishment of a Health Service Commission, as envisaged in the White Paper by the Health Reform Commission,” he said.
In response to a supplementary question from Datuk Dr Alias Razak (PN-Kuala Nerus) on comprehensive reforms through the SPK following the resignation of 3,510 medical officers between 2024 and 2026, he said the MOH had created a special quota of up to 30 per cent for opportunities to pursue specialist studies, specifically for medical officers serving in Sabah and Sarawak.
“We hope this commission will be able to resolve the legacy issues that I have inherited for so long. But today, we have already put in place several foundations for solutions, including increasing permanent positions,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Govt initiates legal action against Zetrix AI over unpaid JPJ revenue, rejected RM231m cheque
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — The government is taking civil legal action against collection agent Zetrix AI Berhad after the company failed to remit millions in government revenue collected on behalf of the Road Transport Department (JPJ).
Transport Minister Anthony Loke said the legal action followed the company’s failure to settle its total outstanding balance and accrued late-payment penalties within the stipulated deadline.
“Any delay in remitting the funds is categorised as a serious breach of contract terms,” Loke said when winding up his ministry’s Budget 2027 second reading debate.
“The government has also established full settlement of all outstanding balances, including late-transfer penalties, as an absolute prerequisite before granting any approval for extension or further operational consideration,” he added.
“We are currently in the process of taking legal action, including filing a civil lawsuit against the company, following its failure to settle the total outstanding amount along with penalties within the stipulated timeframe.”
JPJ initiated follow-up actions between May 19 and October 4, issuing 35 reminder notices and holding four engagement sessions, alongside special discussions, to demand the unremitted revenue.
Loke said that after repeated warnings, the company submitted a post-dated RHB Bank Berhad cheque dated September 30, 2026, valued at RM231 million. The cheque was intended to settle outstanding revenue collected up to August 17, but could not be honoured.
JPJ formally terminated its services with Zetrix AI as a revenue collection agent effective October 5. JPJ subsequently lodged a police report on October 7 over the unremitted government revenue.
To prevent similar issues in the future, Loke said the Transport Ministry and JPJ were tightening internal controls, including upgrading the MySIKAP portal and MyJPJ super app to reduce reliance on third-party collection agents.
The government is also reviewing a proposed mechanism with the Ministry of Finance and the Accountant-General’s Department to route all revenue directly into Treasury accounts without passing through third-party intermediaries, he added.

Title: Singapore to update solar roadmap to meet 4GWp target by 2035
Article:
SINGAPORE, Oct 27 — Singapore will update its Solar Photovoltaic (PV) Roadmap to support its new target of deploying 4 gigawatt-peak (GWp) of solar capacity by 2035, the Energy Market Authority (EMA) said.
EMA said it would collaborate with the Solar Energy Research Institute of Singapore (SERIS) to refresh the roadmap, which was last updated in 2020.
“The refreshed roadmap will assess solar deployment opportunities across diverse types of surfaces and help chart the pathways towards maximising solar deployment over the medium to long term, in support of Singapore’s higher solar ambition,” it said in a statement on Tuesday.
EMA is also taking steps to encourage greater solar adoption for private residential landed properties to unlock more opportunities for solar deployment.
The authority inked a memorandum of understanding with the Sustainable Energy Association of Singapore (SEAS) to explore the development of a one-stop digital portal to make it easier for homeowners to adopt solar.
It will also embark on a research collaboration with the Energy Research Institute @ NTU to study and map the capacity of local electricity networks.
Meanwhile, EMA has awarded grants totalling S$14.9 million (RM47.68 milliona) to four industry projects that will develop and test practical solutions across four areas to strengthen the resilience of Singapore’s electricity grid.
EMA said the projects would improve the maintenance and operation of grid infrastructure, manage the impact of growing distributed energy resources, provide new forms of support for system stability and enable distributed resources to contribute more actively to grid operations. — Bernama

Title: Johor man with six previous criminal and drug-related offences arrested over axe murder of 68-year-old Felda settler
Article:
KOTA TINGGI, Oct 27 — Police arrested a 41-year-old man suspected of hacking a settler to death with an axe at Felda Lok Heng Selatan last night.
Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad said the suspect was arrested by a joint team from the state contingent and district police at a palm oil plantation here at 10.26am today.
“Police seized a motorcycle and an axe from the suspect.
“Investigators believe that the axe was the murder weapon,” he said in a statement today.
Ab Rahaman added that background checks revealed that the local suspect had six previous criminal and drug-related offences.
The incident occurred at 7.56pm last night, when a 68-year-old Felda settler was found covered in blood, with slash wounds to his head and both arms.
The victim was pronounced dead by medical officers dispatched from the nearby Bukit Waha Health Clinic.
Earlier, the axe-wielding suspect was reportedly on a violent rampage before encountering the victim by the roadside.
Ab Rahaman said the suspect, who is in police custody, would be brought to the Pengerang Magistrate’s Court tomorrow for a remand application.
He said the case was being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder.
“Investigators are still looking into the motive behind the incident.
