“The public has been urged to refrain from speculating on the case or posting comments that could interfere with the investigative process,” he said.
The incident was widely shared on social media last night, with reports alleging that the axe-wielding suspect had also been seen acting aggressively by the roadside, causing fear among local residents.

Title: ‘Betrayal’: Putrajaya cuts off Penang petrol station over suspected Budi Madani subsidy abuse
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — Putrajaya has cut off a petrol station in Sungai Buaya, Nibong Tebal, Penang, from the Budi Madani fuel subsidy over suspected misuse that allegedly involved customers’ MyKad details being used without their knowledge.
The Finance Ministry said its checks, triggered by police reports lodged by affected recipients, found more than 1,000 manual-bypass transactions involving over 100,000 litres of petrol and more than RM270,000 in subsidies.
“Any subsidy misuse is a betrayal of the goal of targeting subsidies, even more so while the conflict in West Asia continues to disrupt global energy supply and pressure fuel prices,” the ministry said in a statement today.
It has barred the station from selling subsidised RON95 and diesel under Budi Madani.
It did not name the petrol station.
The ministry is also withholding the station’s subsidy payments, initially more than RM270,000 and subject to further adjustment.
Nine people, including the station owner and family members, have been blocked from using the Budi Madani subsidy while follow-up action is carried out.
The ministry said it is also going through the transaction records of other individuals suspected of being linked to the case, and will act against them if they are found to have abused the subsidy.
“The government will not hesitate to take firm action against any petrol station or consumer found to have breached the Budi Madani guidelines,” it said.

Title: LPT3 highway from Terengganu to Kelantan to proceed via competitive bidding, says Nanta
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — The 122-kilometre East Coast Expressway Phase 3 (LPT3) will be implemented through privatisation under a public-private partnership (PPP) arrangement via a competitive bidding process or Request for Proposal (RFP), with the successful bidder bearing the full development cost.
Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said the proposed alignment, stretching from Kampung Gemuruh in Terengganu to Tunjong in Kelantan, would complement LPT1 and LPT2 in connecting Pahang, Terengganu and Kelantan.
He said the project’s Statement of Needs (SON) had been submitted to the Public Private Partnership Unit (UKAS) under the Prime Minister’s Department to prepare the RFP documents before they are submitted to the Cabinet for consideration and a decision.
“The proposal is currently at the RFP document preparation stage,” he said when winding up the debate on the Supply Bill 2027 (Budget 2027) at the policy stage for the Works Ministry in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Nanta said the government’s current priority was to ensure that the Central Spine Road (LTU) and Kota Bharu-Kuala Krai Highway (KBKK) projects progressed smoothly and were completed on schedule.
For the 70.4-kilometre KBKK project, he said overall physical progress had reached 78.80 per cent, with the Pasir Hor-Kadok stretch fully completed. The remaining five packages are under construction and are expected to be completed in 2027.
The Kelantan section of the LTU, comprising 10 sub-packages worth RM3.08 billion from Kuala Krai to Gua Musang, is expected to be fully completed by 2028, he added.
On delays to LTU Package 3, involving Sections 3B and 3C, Nanta said the appointment of a replacement contractor was in the final stage of the procurement process.
“The Letter of Acceptance is targeted for issuance by mid-November 2026, subject to Finance Ministry approval. This will allow construction work to resume and the remaining work to be completed according to the revised schedule,” he said.
Meanwhile, Nanta said four of the 35 work packages under the 706-kilometre Pan Borneo Highway Sabah project had been completed, while the remaining 31 were targeted for completion in stages by 2030.
He said physical progress had reached 89.54 per cent for Phase 1A and 25.53 per cent for Phase 1B.
For 2027, the Works Ministry has been allocated RM1.146 billion for operating expenditure, an increase of 5.6 per cent, and RM9.736 billion for development expenditure, up 3.0 per cent from RM9.607 billion in 2026. — Bernama

Title: Nik Nazmi spends four hours at Jais, now waits to hear if he will be charged
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Oct 27 — Bersama co-founder Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad spent more than four hours at the Selangor Islamic Religious Department here today, giving his statement over the
khalwat
case.
Berita Harian
reported that the former minister arrived at its headquarters here about 9.15am in a white shirt, black blazer and face mask, and left at 1.30pm.
“From the investigation side, we have given our cooperation, so we are waiting to see whether charges will be filed or not,” his Syarie lawyer, Muhammad Amirul Ashraf A. Ghani, told reporters outside the building.
That decision, he said, rests with the Selangor Syariah Prosecution Department.
Khalwat
is a Syariah offence in which an unmarried Muslim man and woman are found alone together in a secluded place or in close proximity.
Muhammad Amirul Ashraf said his client’s appearance was to complete the investigation under Section 29 of the Syariah Criminal Offences (Selangor) Enactment 1995.
He said statements from Nik Nazmi and the woman linked to the case were taken separately.
Asked whether action could be taken against the person accused of tailing Nik Nazmi and later spreading a video of the episode, the lawyer said the matter would be raised at a later stage.
The department – better known as Jais, the acronym for its Malay name, Jabatan Agama Islam Selangor – confirmed through its director Datuk Mohd Shahzihan Ahmad that Nik Nazmi was at its headquarters, but he declined to comment further.
Nik Nazmi confirmed on October 17 that he was one of two people detained by Jais in Petaling Jaya two days earlier while with a woman who is not a close relative.
The 44-year-old has since been suspended from all official Bersama activities for three months.

Title: Pahang allocates RM3.78m for monsoon preparations, sends aid supplies to 167 forward bases
Article:
KUANTAN, Oct 27 — The Pahang state government has allocated more than RM3 million to prepare for the 2026/2027 Northeast Monsoon (MTL), including the early delivery of aid supplies to 167 forward bases statewide.
Pahang Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail said the state government, through the Pahang Social Welfare Department (JKM), had coordinated a total allocation of RM3,785,115.30 for dry food supplies, logistics, transportation and labour costs across 11 districts.
He said 332,906 units of dry food supplies, comprising nine basic food items weighing a total of 225.11 tonnes, would be distributed to the forward bases from today until Nov 14.
“These include five-kilogram bags of imported Super rice, one-kilogram packs of granulated sugar, two-kilogram packs of cooking oil, 400-gram packs of iodised white salt, Kopi-O bags, tea bags, sardines, chicken curry and assorted biscuits,” he said in a statement today.
He said early logistical preparations were crucial, particularly for remote areas at high risk of being cut off by road, such as upstream areas in the Jerantut and Lipis districts, as well as island areas such as Pulau Tioman in Rompin.
Wan Rosdy also expressed appreciation for the concerted efforts of the Pahang Social Welfare Department, District Disaster Management Committees and rescue agencies in ensuring a robust aid supply chain to safeguard the people of the state.
The statement said the distribution of supplies was determined exclusively based on historical flood impact data.
“Jerantut received the highest allocation among the districts, amounting to RM1,062,893.50, due to the logistical complexities of upstream areas. This was followed by Temerloh at RM962,153 and Rompin, including preparations for a dedicated logistics store on Pulau Tioman, at RM638,782,” it said.
It added that the food supplies would benefit more than 65,000 flood victims. All items meet verified market specifications, are monitored for shelf life and have a long storage life. — Bernama

Title: Crocodile snatches 13-year-old in Sarawak, rescue teams launch search
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 27 — A teenage boy is still missing after he was attacked by a crocodile in Ulu Sungai Plaie, Sebuyau on Monday afternoon.
The Sarawak Fire and Rescue Department (Bomba) said it was notified of the incident at around 7pm.
Bomba Sarawak said Simunjan fire station personnel are currently at the scene conducting a search and rescue (SAR) operation for the boy.
In a Facebook post, licensed crocodile hunters Sarawak Crocter said the attack occurred at around 4pm when the victim was loading oil palm fruits into a boat.
It quoted Simunjan police chief DSP Rafhan Kepli as saying the 13-year-old victim was working with his uncle when the attack occurred.
The page also reported that Balai Ringin incumbent Datuk Snowdan Lawan was at the scene to monitor the SAR operation. — The Borneo Post
*Editor’s note: Bomba is the Malay word for fire and rescue services.

Title: Nearly 72pc of major hospitals record bed waiting times under eight hours, says Dzulkefly
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) is stepping up short- and long-term measures to ease overcrowding and reduce patient waiting times at public healthcare facilities nationwide.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad said sustained efforts were showing positive results, with nearly 72 per cent of major hospitals nationwide reporting average waiting times for beds of under eight hours as of June, compared with 55 per cent in the previous year.
As of June 2026, 28 of the country’s 39 Type 1 and Type 2 hospitals, or 71.8 per cent, recorded average waiting times of less than eight hours for admission from Emergency Departments. These hospitals include state hospitals and major specialist hospitals that handle high numbers of emergency patients and referrals from surrounding districts.
“Relatively speaking, this represents an improvement on 2025, when 55.26 per cent of the hospitals involved recorded an average bed waiting time of less than 480 minutes,” he said during a question-and-answer session in the Dewan Rakyat today.
He was responding to Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun (PH-Port Dickson), who asked how many government hospitals were experiencing ongoing congestion in their Emergency Departments, how long patients waited on average for treatment and ward admission, and what concrete steps the ministry was taking to resolve the problem and ensure prompt treatment.
Dzulkefly added that 94 of 103 Type 3 and Type 4 hospitals (91.3 per cent), including minor specialist hospitals and hospitals without specialists, had average bed waiting times under four hours.
On efforts to ease congestion at major hospitals, he said one short-term measure was the Hospital Services Outsourcing Program (HSOP).
“Since 2024, the HSOP has provided 14 outsourced services, including nephrology and cardiology, benefiting more than 50,000 patients at 75 MOH hospitals,” he said, describing it as a short-term measure.
As part of a comprehensive patient management strategy, the ministry is also strengthening Lean Healthcare initiatives, establishing Bed Management Units (BDUs), expanding day-care services and adopting the hospital cluster approach.
Responding to a supplementary question from Roslan Hashim (PN-Kulim-Bandar Baharu) on alternative measures to ease congestion at healthcare facilities, Dzulkefly said the MOH was actively exploring pilot projects involving the cottage hospital concept and step-down care.
“This includes a step-down care approach, under which patients are transferred to district hospitals once they are confirmed to be stable, without compromising the quality of care.
“We are also reviewing the cottage hospital concept, particularly for rural areas, as practised in the UK and other countries. In Sabah, Sarawak and Peninsular Malaysia, clinics with the capacity and demand could be upgraded to provide inpatient care,” he said.
He said the MOH was also looking into implementing Integrated Clinical Care Management and global surgery, which would allow hospitals without specialists to carry out selected surgical procedures for uncomplicated cases, reducing patient congestion at larger hospitals. — Bernama

Title: Ramanan: More funding being considered for Uyarvu Madani to help small Indian entrepreneurs
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 27 — The government, through the Malaysian Indian Transformation Unit (MITRA), will consider applying for additional funding to expand assistance to small entrepreneurs, particularly those in the B40 and M40 groups who are in need, through the Uyarvu Madani programme following the extraordinary response to applications for the programme.
Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said the government will also examine other sources of financing, including collaboration through other agencies, to help more entrepreneurs expand their businesses.
“We received 8,368 applications for Uyarvu Madani, but we can only grant it to about 780 recipients. If the total number for Phase 1 and Phase 2 is taken into account, we might be able to help around 1,100 to 1,150 entrepreneurs.
“The over 8,000 applications that we have received are a significant number, and this clearly shows that many small entrepreneurs, including B40 entrepreneurs who are striving to advance, need this assistance,” he said at a press conference for the launch of the Harmoni Madani and Dharma Madani programmes here today.
Ramanan said that assistance through Uyarvu Madani is provided via grants, unlike the facilities through Amanah Ikhtiar Malaysia and the Indian Community Entrepreneur Development Scheme (SPUMI) under Tekun Nasional, which are in the form of loans.
Therefore, he said, the selection of recipients will prioritise those who truly need assistance and don’t have access to loans, yet their businesses still have the potential to succeed.
He added that monitoring is also carried out to help recipients overcome any shortcomings or problems that arise in managing their businesses.
Uyarvu MADANI is one of six new initiatives under MITRA for 2026, involving a total allocation of RM65.5 million. — Bernama

Title: MMEA officer killed, two injured during operation in Kuala Perlis waters
Article:
KANGAR, Oct 27 — One member of the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) was killed while two other members were injured during an operation at Sungai Padang, in Kuala Perlis waters, near here, last night.
Kangar district police chief ACP Yusharifuddin Mohd Yusop, when contacted by Bernama, confirmed that the incident occurred yesterday at around 11 pm, however, he said that further information regarding the incident can only be released by the MMEA.
“I can only confirm receiving the report of this incident, but further information regarding this incident can only be released by the MMEA,” he said.
It is understood that the MMEA is expected to hold a press conference about the incident this afternoon. — Bernama

Title: Sarawak Assembly dissolution notification sent to EC, says Speaker
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 27 — A notification letter on the dissolution of the Sarawak State Legislative Assembly has been sent to the Election Commission (EC) today, said Speaker Tan Sri Mohamad Asfia Awang Nassar.
He said he had received the declaration of the dissolution of the state assemby, signed by Sarawak Governor Tun Dr Wan Junaidi Tuanku Jaafar on Friday (Oct 23)
“The declaration of dissolution is also in accordance with Article 21(2) of the State Constitution, which empowers the Governor of Sarawak to dissolve the state assembly.
“As such, I have informed EC chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun of the matter through a letter dated today,” he told a press conference at the State Legislative Assembly building today.
On Oct 23, Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg announced that the State Legislative Assembly would be dissolved on Monday (Oct 26), paving the way for the 13th state election.
Abang Johari, who is also Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) chairman, said that during this period, the state government will discharge its responsibilities in a caretaker capacity, observing the applicable constitutional requirements and conventions.
The current term of the 82-seat Sarawak State Legislative Assembly is due to expire in February 2027.
GPS won 76 of the 82 seats contested in the 12th Sarawak State Election on Dec 18, 2021, while Parti Sarawak Bersatu (PSB) took four seats and DAP secured two.
The state’s political landscape changed after PSB was dissolved in 2024, when three of its former state assemblymen joined the Progressive Democratic Party (PDP), a component party of GPS.
Another former PSB assemblyman, See Chee How, who represents Batu Lintang, subsequently left the party to sit as an Independent.
GPS comprises Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB), Sarawak United Peoples’ Party (SUPP), Parti Rakyat Sarawak (PRS) and PDP. — Bernama

Title: Anwar defends bigger development allocations for Sabah, Sarawak, cites infrastructure needs
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — The government has defended its decision to provide larger development allocations for Sabah and Sarawak, citing their geographical challenges and infrastructure needs.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said these needs included the poor condition of roads in several areas of Sabah, despite its smaller population compared with other states.
“We should not look at this from the perspective of just one state when it comes to addressing the needs of Sabah and Sarawak.
“No, the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) must be viewed as a national covenant. It is in our collective interest to safeguard the interests of everyone,” he said in response to a supplementary question from Datuk Seri Dr Ronald Kiandee (PN-Beluran) during the Ministers’ Question Time in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Ronald sought clarification on the decision to reduce or withhold allocations for certain projects in Sabah and Sarawak under the Ministry of Rural and Regional Development (KKDW), despite the two states being entitled to greater allocations under MA63. He also raised the possibility that the decision was influenced by political differences.
In response, Anwar said the development allocations for Sabah and Sarawak announced in Budget 2027 did not include expenditure for the projects under KKDW raised by the MP.
“What we announced were projects approved based on the latest assessments,” he said.
Anwar said the government acknowledged that development allocations would not be sufficient to meet every need, but stressed that good governance must be ensured to prevent leakages.
He said procurement processes and contract awards also needed to be scrutinised to ensure compliance with regulations and take into account the capacity to implement the projects. — Bernama

Title: Anwar plans new law for GLCs and GLICs, cites Battersea losses and eFishery failure
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — The government plans to introduce legislation to tighten governance at government-linked companies (GLCs) and government-linked investment companies (GLICs), Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
He said the proposed law would set clearer, stricter rules, including limits on the powers and responsibilities of those leading the entities.
“Past experience has shown both strengths and weaknesses. These issues have been documented in Royal Commissions of Inquiry (RCIs), task force reports and White Papers on 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) and Felda, as well as in cases involving Tabung Haji. The breaches were numerous and clearly excessive, making them difficult to defend,” he said during the Prime Minister’s Question Time in the Dewan Rakyat.
He was responding to a supplementary question from Syahredzan Johan (DAP-Bangi) on measures to improve governance at GLCs, GLICs and statutory bodies to prevent a recurrence of scandals involving 1MDB and Tabung Haji.
Anwar said clear rules were also needed for subsidiaries of government agencies, adding that the government had not identified governance breaches on the scale previously seen at 1MDB and Tabung Haji.
Efforts to impose tighter controls had faced strong resistance from political and business elites accustomed to old practices, making political will essential to address the problem, he said.
“Governance must be strengthened, and the powers of those appointed to lead these entities must be clearly limited. They must be held accountable and must not treat these institutions as their personal or family property,” he said.
Earlier, Syahredzan had asked Anwar to explain why government departments, GLICs, GLCs and statutory bodies were involved in development projects, and how this could address public concerns without compromising their core mandates and responsibilities.
Anwar said investments by GLICs and GLCs helped local companies expand and attract private investment from domestic and foreign investors.
He cited Khazanah Nasional Bhd’s Dana Impak, which has invested RM2.6 billion since its establishment in 2021.
Khazanah initially acquired a 30 per cent stake in local dairy company Farm Fresh Bhd before it went public at a valuation of RM2.5 billion, Anwar said. Khazanah later divested its stake after the company had established itself.
Budget 2027 also allocated RM450 million through Jelawang Capital, Khazanah and the Retirement Fund Inc’s (KWAP) Dana Perintis to develop start-ups, he added.
Anwar also called for closer scrutiny of overseas investments to avoid a repeat of the Battersea Power Station redevelopment project in Britain.
He said the initial investment had been too high and incurred losses, although efforts were under way to recover the investment.
He was responding to a supplementary question from Hassan Karim (PKR-Pasir Gudang) on the amount invested by GLCs and GLICs in the Battersea redevelopment in London and its benefits to Malaysia’s economy.
Anwar said KWAP, Khazanah and Permodalan Nasional Bhd continued to seek investment opportunities at home and abroad.
However, the government had prioritised domestic investments over the past three years, setting an initial target of channelling at least 20 per cent of investments into Malaysia, he said.
The proportion would rise depending on the readiness and capacity of the institutions concerned, he added.
Anwar said most overseas investments had generated substantial returns, although some had incurred losses.
On KWAP’s investment in eFishery, he said the failed investment should not be taken as representative of the fund’s overall performance, noting that KWAP had recorded RM8 billion in profits. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: KWAP stands for Kumpulan Wang Persaraan (Diperbadankan) in Malay, or Retirement Fund Inc in English.

Title: Anwar calls for stricter rules for GLCs, says bosses must not treat them as family property
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — The government is considering a Government-Owned Entities Bill to tighten governance at government-linked companies (GLCs) and related agencies, and prevent misappropriation such as that seen in 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB), Felda and Tabung Haji.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the proposed law would set clearer rules and ensure government-owned entities, including their subsidiaries, were subject to effective oversight.
He said weaknesses and serious breaches in the management of government institutions had been highlighted in Royal Commissions of Inquiry (RCIs), task force reports and white papers.
“Our proposal to table the Bill is not only for (strengthening) governance, but also to establish very clear rules and laws for regulatory purposes.
“That is why I believe the Bill will establish strict measures… even for GLCs, governance must be tightened. Those vested with authority and the figures appointed to these positions must be more accountable and must not treat these entities as property belonging to themselves or their families,” he said during Ministers’ Question Time in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Anwar was responding to a supplementary question from Syahredzan Johan (PH-Bangi) on measures to strengthen corporate governance at GLCs and statutory bodies to prevent a recurrence of misappropriation involving government institutions.
Anwar said oversight of subsidiaries was one weakness that needed to be addressed, as they were not necessarily subject to the same controls as their parent agencies.
He said efforts to strengthen governance also faced resistance from vested-interest groups, including political elites and businesspeople accustomed to past practices.
Anwar stressed that political figures were prohibited from interfering in GLC and government-linked investment company (GLIC) project selection and investment priorities.
Instead, investment decisions must be made by investment bodies comprising professionals and people with relevant expertise, he said.
He said this was crucial to ensuring prudent investment decisions, particularly in light of past governance failures. — Bernama

Title: RM1,000 per attack? Perak police arrest three teens over arson, paint-splashing cases across four states
Article:
IPOH, Oct 27 — Three 19-year-old men have been arrested in Penang over alleged arson and paint-splashing attacks on homes across several states, with police saying they were offered RM500 to RM1,000 per incident.
Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said Taiping police arrested the three men at separate locations in Penang between 5pm and 9pm on October 22, and had helped solve nine vandalism cases across four states: two in Perak, three in Kedah, two in Johor, one in Penang and one in Selangor.
“The first suspect, a college student, was arrested in Tanjung Bungah, where police seized a mobile phone, clothing believed to have been worn during an incident and a grey Proton X70,” he told a press conference at Perak Police Headquarters here.
“The second suspect, a storekeeper, was arrested in Taman Sri Rambai, Bukit Mertajam, where police seized a mobile phone, clothing and a white Nissan Teana. The third suspect, also a college student, was arrested in Taman Machang Bubok, where police seized a mobile phone and a black Honda City.”
Mohd Alwi said preliminary investigations found that the suspects had no previous criminal records and had admitted to carrying out the attacks after being offered payment by an unidentified person they contacted only through WhatsApp.
Police are investigating two cases in Taiping.
In the first, reported on September 19, two men allegedly splashed red paint on a house in Taman Pura Jaya, Simpang, before throwing a bottle containing petrol and setting it alight towards the property.
This case is being investigated under Section 435 of the Penal Code for mischief by fire.
In the second case reported on October 10, two men allegedly splashed red paint on houses in Taman Sri Larut, Simpang, and a neighbouring property.
This case is being investigated under Section 427 of the Penal Code for mischief, which carries a prison term of one to five years, a fine, or both, while Section 435 provides for imprisonment of up to 14 years and a possible fine.

Title: Love is in the air, and so is the bill: 13pc of Malaysian men willing to go into debt for dates
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — For some Malaysian men, keeping the romance alive could mean stretching their wallets — and a new study suggests some are even willing to go into debt for a date.
According to research by Legasi Research, men continue to shoulder most dating expenses, with 59.3 per cent saying they usually pay the entire bill, compared with just 8.2 per cent of women.
“The data shows that the majority of men still bear the dating expenses, highlighting a strong adherence to traditional gender roles in courtship,” Legasi Research economic researcher Firdzan Nur Yassin, said today in a news conference here to present the findings.
Dinner dates and the price of romance
Shopping malls remain a popular dating destination, with 44.1 per cent of respondents saying they frequent them, while 42.8 per cent opt for cafes or restaurants.
Food and drinks are the biggest expense, cited by 92.8 per cent of respondents, while a typical date costs between RM51 and RM200.
But the bill is not always easy to swallow, with 49.3 per cent of respondents describing dating costs as “expensive”.
Men also appear more likely to feel the financial strain, with 27.5 per cent reporting pressure from dating expenses, compared with 16.4 per cent of women.
Picking up the tab — and taking turns
The findings suggest that splitting costs is more common among women, with 50.8 per cent saying they take turns paying and 32.8 per cent saying their partner usually covers the bill.
For men, the willingness to spend more appears tied to keeping a relationship going, with 79.1 per cent saying they would increase their spending to maintain their romantic connection.
First dates can bring added pressure to impress, with 59.3 per cent of men saying they are willing to spend more on them, compared with 23 per cent of women.
That willingness, however, has its limits — or at least it can come at a cost.
The study found that 13.2 per cent of men were willing to incur debt for a date, compared with 4.9 per cent of women.
Legasi Research economic researcher Firdzan Nur Yassin speaks to the press during the briefing session on Dating Expenses here at Ideas Hotel, Kuala Lumpur on October 27, 2026. — Picture by Sayuti Zainudin
Young hearts, tight budgets
The survey respondents were largely young, with 43.4 per cent aged between 18 and 24, while 53.3 per cent lived in Selangor or Kuala Lumpur.
A substantial proportion reported monthly incomes below RM3,000, making regular dating another expense to juggle alongside everyday living costs.
Most respondents said they went on dates at least once a month, adding to the pressure on those trying to balance their love lives with their budgets.
The research used random sampling to collect 160 surveys nationwide, of which 152 were deemed suitable for analysis.
Thirty per cent of respondents were married, with the researchers including their outings in the definition of “dating” to capture a broader picture of romantic spending.

Title: Transferred Perak principal now under police probe after mother reports alleged sexual harassment of her Form Three daughter
Article:
IPOH, Oct 27 — Police are investigating alleged sexual harassment involving a school principal and a Form Three student in Hutan Melintang, Perak, following a report by the student’s mother.
Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the report was lodged on October 24, with the case being investigated under Section 15(a) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017.
“Following the report lodged by the victim’s mother, the case is being investigated under Section 15(a) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017,” he told a press conference at the Perak Police Headquarters today.
Mohd Alwi said the 56-year-old principal lodged a separate report the next day, alleging that he had been assaulted by members of the student’s family after a video of their confrontation went viral.
Police are investigating the alleged assault under Section 323 of the Penal Code, which covers voluntarily causing hurt, and alleged misuse of network facilities under Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998.
“Our investigation found that the victim’s family confronted the principal following allegations that he had contacted the student and expressed his love and affection for her, as reported previously,” Mohd Alwi said.
He said police had recorded statements from nine people, including the principal, and would investigate the matter thoroughly as it involved a civil servant.
On October 25, Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said she had directed the Perak Education Department to investigate the allegations and that the principal had been temporarily transferred to the Bagan Datuk District Education Office pending the probe.
Hutan Melintang is a district under Bagan Datuk.
The case came to public attention after a social media post warned parents and residents about allegations that a principal at a government secondary school had sent romantic messages to a Form Three student.
A video circulated alongside the claims showed a man believed to be the principal being confronted by several women.

Title: Anwar defends GLIC-funded housing, says Petronas helped develop Putrajaya
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today defended the use of government-linked investment companies (GLICs) to fund domestic development, citing Petronas’ role in Putrajaya and arguing that public needs can be balanced with commercial returns.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, said that the national oil company had helped fund Putrajaya’s development through Putrajaya Holdings, which encompasses government offices, public amenities, hotels, commercial ventures and tourism facilities.
“Putrajaya was developed with Petronas funds from the outset,” he told the Dewan Rakyat during Prime Minister’s Question Time.
Anwar was responding to Bangi MP Syahredzan Johan who asked for the rationale for involving government agencies, GLICs, GLCs and statutory bodies in development projects while safeguarding their core mandates and responsibilities.
Anwar said the Kota Madani housing project was intended to address a shortage of accommodation for civil servants in Putrajaya, with 80 per cent of its units reserved for them.
He said GLICs had also invested in student accommodation for Malaysians in Canada, South Korea, the Netherlands and the United Kingdom, arguing that such investments should be expanded domestically.
“So why can this not be expanded in Malaysia?” he asked.
Anwar said the first phase of a student accommodation initiative would involve 10,000 units, with a longer-term target of 30,000 units involving GLICs.
“It is not merely about helping people; it is also about serving commercial needs and interests,” he said.
He said the initiatives formed part of efforts to strengthen domestic economic resilience, while GLICs were expected to consider national priorities alongside investment returns.
Anwar said GLICs had committed RM120 billion in domestic direct investments from 2024 to 2028, in addition to RM440 billion already invested in the domestic public market.
He also cited the Kampung Angkat and Sekolah Angkat Madani programmes, which he said covered 500 villages and 1,700 schools with support from GLICs and private companies.

Title: Fake hospital calls, bogus investments and loan scams: Police arrest 36 in Perak
Article:
IPOH, Oct 27 — Perak police have busted three scam syndicates targeting Malaysian, Chinese and Japanese victims in separate raids in Ipoh and Kampar, arresting 36 people.
Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said five Japanese men, aged 21 to 27, were arrested at a two-storey house in Kampung Simee at about 6.10pm on October 26 for allegedly impersonating staff from a Japanese hospital.
“An analysis of the devices found that the syndicate had been impersonating staff from a Japanese hospital, claiming victims’ family members had been involved in accidents and required emergency surgery,” he told a press conference at the Perak Police Headquarters today.
The syndicate allegedly demanded payment through Signal and used Japanese bank accounts to receive the money. Police seized 16 mobile phones, seven iPads and two routers worth RM22,500. The group had allegedly been operating since late September.
In a second raid at a factory in Bercham at about 12.05am on October 23, police arrested 25 Chinese nationals, including a woman, aged 26 to 41, over an alleged fake investment scheme targeting Chinese victims.
“The syndicate was using TikTok to promote the scheme before directing interested investors to Telegram for further communication,” Mohd Alwi said.
Victims were directed to the syndicate’s platform and asked to invest between 99 and 199 yuan.
The suspects allegedly recruited customers for a promised monthly salary of RM8,000.
Police seized 25 computers and four routers worth RM25,000.
All 25 were remanded for seven days from October 23 to 29.
In a third raid at two apartments in Bandar Agacia, Kampar, at about 6.30pm on October 22, police arrested five local men and a Thai woman, aged 19 to 30, over an alleged fake loan scam.
“Victims were asked to send their ATM cards and PINs by post as collateral to secure the loans. The syndicate then used the victims’ ATM cards to carry out online scams,” Mohd Alwi said.
Police seized 13 mobile phones and six ATM cards worth RM15,000. The syndicate had allegedly operated since June, recruiting agents through Facebook and paying them RM3,000 to RM5,000 a month.
Its bank accounts were also linked to five fake loan scam cases in Selangor, Kuala Lumpur, Johor and Sabah, while student apartments in Kampar were allegedly used as its base.
Mohd Alwi said the cases were being investigated for cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property under Section 420 of the Penal Code, and criminal conspiracy under Section 120B.
Those convicted could face up to 10 years’ imprisonment, whipping and a fine.

Title: Buy low, sell high: Kelantan shoppers see opportunity as gold falls to RM503
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Oct 27 — Shoppers have been streaming into Kelantan’s gold shops to snap up jewellery as prices sag to about RM503 a gramme yesterday, the
New Straits Times
reported today.
Many shops around Pasar Siti Khadijah in the Kelantan capital here were crowded with customers, with gold priced between RM503 and RM504 a gramme, according to the newspaper.
“Whenever prices drop, I take the opportunity to buy more for my collection,” Halima Osman, 45, a customer at one of the shops, told the newspaper.
She said the fall was sharper than she expected, as prices had earlier approached RM600 a gramme.
Halima bought a bracelet today, saying that she had been tracking the price slide for weeks and believed RM503 was the lowest so far.
“We buy when prices are low and sell when they rise to make a profit,” she added.
Gold is deeply rooted in Kelantan, where women have long treated it as both savings and business capital, with monthly sales in the state estimated at about 500kg, the
New Straits Times
reported previously.
Another shopper, Nur Ain Abdul Manaf, 30, left with a necklace and an anklet.
She said she had long treated gold jewellery as a form of savings and investment that could be sold if she needed cash later.
“While I was at the jewellery shop, everyone was there to buy, not sell,” she said.
Spot gold rose 0.3 per cent to US$4,007.57 (RM16,351) an ounce yesterday after hitting US$3,975 (RM16,218) when markets closed on Friday, its lowest level since July 20, according to
Business Recorder.
Kelantan saw similar scenes in June, when
The Star
reported that the decline in the price of 916 gold prompted many people returning to Kota Bharu for the Hari Raya Puasa holiday to buy jewellery.
The gold-buying craze is also happening worldwide.
Bargain hunters also packed Shenzhen’s Shuibei gold market after a dip in global prices,
Business Times
reported today while gold traded at a premium in India for the first time in more than three months as a price pullback boosted jewellery purchases,
Reuters
reported.

Title: Lorry driver claims microsleep caused crash that injured two journalists in Perak
Article:
IPOH, Oct 27 — The lorry driver involved in an accident with two journalists in Menglembu last Sunday claimed that he had experienced a microsleep, which led to the crash, police said.
Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said police were continuing their investigation.
He said the 35-year-old lorry driver tested negative for drugs and had no criminal record.
“The lorry driver has given a statement. Whatever the reason, it is still an offence because he hit the vehicle from behind. We will take the necessary action,” he told a press conference at the Perak police contingent headquarters here today.
Meanwhile, Mohd Alwi said police had yet to secure dashcam footage from any party, adding that the scene was not covered by closed-circuit television (CCTV).
Two journalists, Nur Afiradina Arshad, 34, of the Malaysian National News Agency (Bernama) and Zahratulhayat Mat Arif, 37, of The New Straits Times (NST), were injured when their car collided with a lorry at about 5.45 am last Sunday.
Both were travelling in a Perodua Bezza to cover a programme involving Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi in Bagan Datuk. — Bernama

Title: Adam Adli: Pakatan not fielding ‘token candidate’ in Paya Rumput, banking on Azman’s experience
Article:
MELAKA, Oct 27 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) is banking on the extensive federal administrative experience of its candidate, Datuk Azman Abidin, in the contest for the Paya Rumput seat in the Melaka state election, said acting Melaka PKR chief Adam Adli Abd Halim.
He said the selection of the Prime Minister’s political secretary reflected PH’s commitment to offering an experienced candidate who can understand residents’ needs and translate them into effective solutions.
“Paya Rumput is not a place for a token candidate. We have made sure that the candidate we field has experience, wisdom and, most importantly, knows what needs to be done.
“When we field a figure like Azman, who has an extensive background in the country’s administration, it means we are taking this seriously,” he said at the launch of the Paya Rumput operations room and a meet-and-greet session with party machinery and members of PKR Tangga Batu division here last night.
Also present were Home Minister and PKR vice-president performing the duties of deputy president, Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail, Senator Isaiah Jacob and PKR Tangga Batu chief Azlan Osman.
Adam Adli said Azman’s experience serving at the Prime Minister’s Office had given him exposure to the policymaking and implementation processes, management of government agencies and coordination of allocations.
He said these strengths could help Azman champion the needs of Paya Rumput residents more effectively, particularly in areas involving basic infrastructure development, welfare and community development.
“This close relationship will ensure that the implementation of basic infrastructure projects, welfare issues and community development in Paya Rumput can be expedited without bureaucratic obstacles.
“The progress of an area requires an elected representative who not only turns up to listen to problems, but also has access and avenues to secure quick solutions through the support of the federal government administration,” he said.
The Election Commission has set Nov 14 as polling day for the 16th Melaka State Election, with nomination day on Oct 31 and early voting on Nov 10. — Bernama

Title: Heavy rain, high tides put Pulau Perhentian villagers on alert as monsoon season begins
Article:
JERTIH, Oct 27 — Residents in the village on Pulau Perhentian here have started making early preparations for the Northeast Monsoon (MTL), which is expected to bring heavy rain and pose a flood risk to low-lying areas of the village.
Resident Azizah Ab Rahman, 59, said the village was also vulnerable to flooding, especially when heavy rain coincided with high tides, causing water to stagnate and making it difficult for it to drain into the sea.
“In the past, during the MTL, this situation caused low-lying areas, such as Kampung Tengah, to be flooded up to a depth of almost one metre when rainwater flowing down from the hills could not drain into the sea due to the high tide.
“As a precaution, I began moving household items to higher ground a few days ago, as floods can occur at any time during the monsoon season,” she told Bernama when met at her house on Pulau Perhentian yesterday.
Azizah, who has been living alone since her husband died several years ago, said her children worked and lived on the mainland, leaving her to seek help from neighbours to move heavy items, such as the refrigerator and washing machine, from the kitchen to the higher section of her house.
She said that although the flash floods usually receded within a few hours after the rain stopped, early preparations were important to prevent damage to household items and property losses.
Meanwhile, another resident, 36-year-old Hayatunnupus Nawawi said she had also placed her refrigerator in the living room on a specially built platform about 1.5 metres high to protect it from floodwaters.
“I have kept the refrigerator there permanently since last year’s incident because it is difficult to move it when flooding occurs.
“I have two young children, aged five and nine, while my husband, Ali Abdullah, 36, is physically paralysed,” she said.
Pulau Perhentian Village Development and Security Committee (JPKK) chairman Nik Zawawi Mohd Nor said about 30 houses were usually affected whenever flooding occurred in the village.
He said the floods were generally caused by heavy rain coinciding with high tides during the MTL, making it difficult for water to drain quickly into the sea.
“Flooding usually lasts about two hours and may occur several times throughout the MTL season, depending on rainfall and tidal conditions,” he added. — Bernama

Title: Caretaker mode: What Sarawak’s government can and can’t do
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 27 — With the Sarawak State Legislative Assembly (DUN) officially dissolved on Monday (Oct 26), the state government remains in office in a caretaker capacity. Three legal experts explain the caretaker government’s role, powers and limitations.
Does Sarawak still have a state government after the DUN is dissolved?
The dissolution ends the legislature’s term, but does not automatically remove the state executive.
According to Lawyer Kamek director Simon Siah, Article 6(3) of the Sarawak Constitution provides for executive members to continue holding office, subject to the relevant constitutional requirements.
Ralph Advocates principal Ralph Lee said the Premier and Cabinet would continue to administer the state in a caretaker capacity.
“Under Article 21(4) of the Sarawak Constitution, an election must be held within 60 days of dissolution, while the new DUN must meet within 120 days,” he said.
What is the role of a caretaker government?
Its primary responsibility is to ensure continuity in state administration while avoiding major decisions that could bind the incoming government.
Advocates Association of Sarawak president Gurvir Singh Sandhu said public services, salaries, existing contracts and approved projects would continue.
He added that spending should remain within allocations approved by the DUN, including those under the 2027 Sarawak Budget.
Lee said routine administration and urgent action to protect public safety could proceed, distinguishing these from new initiatives or substantial expansions of existing programmes.
What are the limitations of a caretaker government?
Although its executive powers remain in place, constitutional convention calls for restraint over decisions with significant or long-term consequences.
Siah said the caretaker government should generally avoid major policy changes, defer important appointments and refrain from awarding major contracts or making substantial new financial commitments unless necessary.
Lee said the significance, urgency, reversibility and impact of a decision should be considered to ensure it does not materially bind the next state government.
Is there a specific law governing caretaker governments in Sarawak?
According to the experts, there is no express, comprehensive caretaker-government framework in Sarawak’s Constitution, or a specific written law setting out its powers and limitations.
“Instead, the conduct of a caretaker government is guided by constitutional convention inherited from the Westminster tradition,” said Sandhu.
Adding on, Siah said that conventions were established practices governing how a government should operate, rather than rules directly enforceable by courts.
He said the Premier and Cabinet retained the same executive powers under the Constitution, although convention would call for them to exercise those powers responsibly during the caretaking period.
What happens if a caretaker government breaches these conventions?
A breach of convention alone does not automatically make a government decision unlawful or invalidate it.
“Decisions could still be challenged through judicial review if there were separate legal grounds, such as acting beyond legal powers or for an improper purpose,” said Sandhu.
Lee said the caretaker government must also comply with applicable laws governing public expenditure, procurement and elections.
The experts stressed that restraint was important in protecting public confidence in the electoral process. — The Borneo Post
* Editor’s note: DUN stands for Dewan Undangan Negeri, which is Malay for State Legislative Assembly.

Title: Locked out over maintenance fees? Court says JMBs can’t do that
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 27 — Joint management bodies (JMBs) cannot bar owners from their own units over unpaid maintenance charges, the Court of Appeal has ruled, news outlet
Free Malaysia Today
reported.
The regulations let a JMB deactivate defaulters’ access cards, require them to sign a register when seeking help to enter or leave the building, and suspend their use of common facilities and services, but the court found nothing in them that lets a JMB keep an owner out of his or her own unit.
“The sanction it authorises is an inconvenience and a record. It presupposes entry. It does not authorise exclusion,” Justice Ong Chee Kwan, who delivered the broad grounds, was quoted as saying in court yesterday.
The ruling came in an appeal by SL Land Sdn Bhd and Foong Wei Ching against the JMB managing the Sentral Bazar shopping mall in Nilai, Negeri Sembilan, which had refused to let the company’s directors and authorised agents into their units.
The three-member bench chaired by Datuk Alwi Abdul Wahab, with Datuk Shahnaz Sulaiman and Ong, unanimously allowed the appeal.
The court set aside a High Court ruling that had upheld the JMB’s power to impose conditions on entry by defaulters under the Strata Management (Maintenance and Management) Regulations 2015.
Ong said barring an owner from entering his or her own unit was a far more drastic step than the measures specified in the regulations and interfered with the owner’s right to use and enjoy the property.
He said clear legal provisions would be needed to confer such a power, but none existed.
The Court of Appeal unanimously ruled to allow the appeal filed by SL Land Sdn Bhd and Foong Wei Ching against the joint management body managing the Sentral Bazar shopping mall in Nilai, Negeri Sembilan, which had refused to let the company’s directors and authorised agents into their units. — Picture from Facebook/Sentral Bazar
The court declared unlawful the JMB’s refusals to let SL Land’s directors and authorised agents enter their units on May 4 and June 20, 2023.
It also ruled that requiring the company’s shareholders to be present or consent before entry was not authorised by law.
The judges granted an injunction stopping the JMB from blocking access, while preserving its powers under the regulations and reasonable, non-discriminatory security arrangements that apply to all proprietors.
They set aside the High Court’s RM30,000 costs order and awarded SL Land nominal damages, as the company had not proved any substantial loss.
The JMB was ordered to pay RM50,000 in costs for proceedings in both courts.
Lawyers Ivanpal Singh Grewal, Harwinder Kaur and S. Nisha appeared for SL Land and Foong, while K. Muralidharan and Ahmad Amir Mukhlis represented the JMB.

Title: Zahid urges public to stay alert as northeast monsoon begins today
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has urged the public to stay vigilant and prioritise safety as the 2026/2027 Northeast Monsoon is expected to begin today.
He said the monsoon, expected to persist until March 2027, could bring prolonged heavy rainfall, flooding and rough seas, threatening residents’ safety, particularly in vulnerable areas.
He said the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) forecasts indicated that three to five episodes of prolonged heavy rainfall could occur between November 2026 and January 2027.
“This could increase the risk of flooding, particularly in areas near rivers and low-lying areas,” he said in a Facebook post today.
Ahmad Zahid said strong winds during the period could also cause rough seas and rising sea levels in the South China Sea.
He advised the public to monitor the latest weather forecasts and warnings, avoid flood-prone areas and never attempt to cross floodwaters, while complying with the authorities’ instructions, including evacuation orders when necessary.
Ahmad Zahid also highlighted the importance of being prepared by having important documents, medication, essential supplies and contact numbers ready for emergencies.
“Safety for yourself and your family must come first,” he said, hoping Malaysians would be kept safe from any calamities during the monsoon period. — Bernama

Title: Waze alternatives? Delivery riders, e-hailing drivers wait for TuJu to prove itself
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — For delivery riders and e-hailing drivers who spend hours on the road, switching navigation apps is not as simple as downloading a new one, especially when the routes they take can affect their time, earnings and ability to reach customers.
Outside Sunway Wangsa Walk here, three delivery riders said they had yet to try TuJu, the locally developed navigation app promoted by the government as an alternative to Waze, with some preferring to wait until it becomes more reliable before making the switch.
Muhammad Nabil Khairuddin, 30, a Grab rider, said he first learnt about TuJu through TikTok and Facebook yesterday and was considering downloading it to see how it compared with established navigation apps.
“I might try downloading and using TuJu first to see whether it needs any improvements. I’ll see how it works,” he told
Malay Mail
.
For deliveries, however, Nabil said he already relied on Grab’s in-house navigation system, which allows him to find destinations without leaving the ride-hailing app.
He said Grab previously allowed riders to choose between Waze and Google Maps, but its own navigation system now offered a more convenient option.
“For deliveries, Grab has its own map. Previously, we could choose whether to use Waze or Google Maps, but now Grab has its own navigation system, so there is no need to leave the app. We can navigate directly from there,” he said.
Another rider, who wished to be known as Mat Yo, 32, who works with Lalamove, said he would only consider switching to TuJu once the app was stable, preferring to stick with Waze in the meantime.
“Honestly, Waze is the easiest to use. For Lalamove, it can use Google Maps, but I rarely use it because I’m more comfortable with Waze, it’s easier,” he said.
Mohammad Abdul Aziz Mohd Bhekori, 25, another Grab rider, said he knew little about TuJu and continued to rely on Grab’s map or Google Maps.
Mohammad Abdul Aziz Mohd Bhekori said he knew little about TuJu and continued to rely on Grab’s map or Google Maps. — Picture by Muhammad Yusry
He said he had stopped using Waze previously because it sometimes directed him along what he considered unreasonable routes.
The hesitation among riders comes as the government urges Malaysians to consider uninstalling Waze over concerns that users’ personal and movement data could fall under Israeli jurisdiction.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim on October 20, 2026, encouraged the public to use TuJu, developed by the Malaysian Highway Authority (LLM) in collaboration with Prosignal Consortium Sdn Bhd, as an alternative to Waze.
National Security Council director-general for National Security Raja Datuk Nushirwan Zainal Abidin has urged Malaysians to uninstall Waze over the concerns.
However, he said that there will not be a blanket ban issued to preserve individual freedom of choice.
For e-hailing drivers, the decision also comes down to familiarity and whether a new app can offer the features they have come to depend on.
A Grab driver of a blue Perodua Bezza, who had just dropped off a passenger at the Sri Rampai LRT station and wished to remain anonymous, said he preferred Waze’s navigation system because it showed toll charges upfront.
Having used Waze for years, he said switching to another app would require time to adjust, but he would consider TuJu if other users gave it positive reviews.
“If people start saying that TuJu is good, then I’ll use it,” he said.
Muhammad Khalid Azmi, 28, an e-hailing driver based in Putrajaya, said he had not tried TuJu and would continue using Waze, with Google Maps as an alternative.
Khalid, who has used Waze for more than five years, said he relied on it to check traffic conditions, estimated arrival times and journey durations.
He also found Grab’s navigation system useful, saying it could incorporate community feedback and updates, while the map available on Bolt was less accurate in his experience.
“I haven’t used TuJu yet, so I don’t know what it is like, or what its weaknesses and strengths are. For now, I prefer either Waze or Google Maps because Grab has its own in-house map, which works reasonably well.
“However, when I’m using Bolt, its map is not accurate. The established navigation apps are either Google Maps and Waze. I’m not sure about the other navigation apps, but those two are already linked to e-hailing apps,” he said.
TuJu, which was launched in November last year, provides navigation, estimated arrival times, live traffic information, highway CCTV feeds, toll fares and information on rest and service areas.
However, the app has faced technical disruptions following a surge in users after Anwar recommended it as an alternative to Waze.
LLM and PCSB apologised for the disruption, saying they were working to restore system stability, increase capacity and address complaints about navigation functions, route accuracy and the overall user experience.
Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo said that the government was also expanding TuJu’s coverage beyond highways to include ordinary roads, following public feedback calling for more comprehensive navigation services.
The expansion is intended to improve traffic information and the app’s overall capabilities, as the government seeks to strengthen the use of locally developed technology.
For riders and drivers who depend on navigation throughout the working day, however, TuJu will have to prove itself on the road before it can displace the apps they already know and trust.
